title: Prompt injection hijacks agents and exfiltrates private data
problem: Agents that read untrusted content while holding private data and outbound channels can be hijacked by hidden instructions, and no complete defense exists. Allowlists can be bypassed.
who: builders and users of tool-using and browsing agents
current_solutions: Lockdown Mode, treating LLM output as untrusted, classifiers, URL allowlists, CSP rules, markdown sanitization, BrowseSafe, human approval, egress firewalls
opportunity: Build an agent firewall that scans ingested content, strips hidden instructions, enforces deterministic egress policy and flags lethal-trifecta setups.

title: Routing tasks across models by cost and strength
problem: Different models excel at planning, coding and review, and cheap models suffice for routine work, but users hand-switch between tools.
current_solutions: Manual Claude/Codex handoffs, OpenCode, OpenRouter, per-task effort settings, cheaper subagent models.
opportunity: Build a harness-agnostic router that picks model and effort per task and runs cross-model review.

title: Human review of agent code is the bottleneck
problem: Agents produce diffs and PRs faster than humans can read them, so review caps what ships and bugs slip through. Plain line diffs make it hard to see behavior changes or the agent's reasoning.
who: developers and teams reviewing agent-written PRs
current_solutions: Shorter PR descriptions, AI first-pass reviewers, Devin Review, Claude Code review, small chunked iterations, reviewing specs instead of code.
opportunity: Build review tooling that summarizes agent changes, ranks risk, shows intent and behavior changes, and triages what needs human eyes.

title: Agents falsely claim completion and cheat on tests
problem: Agents report tasks done or verified when they are not, weaken or delete tests, and take shortcuts, forcing users to recheck everything.
who: developers relying on agents for autonomous work
current_solutions: Manual rechecking, stop hooks, TDD prompts, cross-model review, verification subagents, conformance suites, Playwright MCP.
opportunity: Build an independent verification layer that checks agent claims against repo state and real tests, and flags test tampering or faked success.

title: AI-generated code piles up bloat and technical debt
problem: Agent code is duplicated, inconsistent, over-engineered and poorly architected, and complexity sprawls faster than humans notice.
current_solutions: Manual refactoring, cleanup passes, lint-fix agent loops, human-designed architecture, linters and type checkers.
opportunity: Build a continuous auditor and cleanup agent that finds dead code, duplication, and architecture drift and refactors it.

title: Benchmark scores do not match real-world usefulness
problem: Headline scores diverge from daily use, and benchmaxxing erodes trust. Users cannot tell which model is better in practice.
who: developers, model buyers and teams choosing models
current_solutions: Vibe checks, long-session reports, private evals, open-world evals, live-session leaderboards
opportunity: Build real-work benchmarks and independent comparison views grounded in actual usage.

title: Independent third-party audit of frontier labs
problem: Labs self-report incidents and safety claims, auditors lack access and independence, and no one verifies compliance.
current_solutions: Embedded auditors like METR, UK AISI, CAISI pilot, proposed FINRA-style body
opportunity: Offer independent audit, certification and verification services with standardized access and conflict disclosure.

title: Sandboxing and egress control for coding agents
problem: Default sandboxes, containers and allowlists are too permissive and leak through escapes, covert channels and shared infrastructure. Teams lack an enforceable boundary around agent files, network and credentials.
who: developers and teams running coding or local agents on real machines and codebases
current_solutions: nono, SELinux/AppArmor/Landlock, gVisor, microVMs, Wasm, Claude Cowork VM, NVIDIA OpenShell, NemoClaw, egress proxies and allowlists, throwaway copies
opportunity: Build a turnkey agent runtime with OS-level isolation, default-deny egress, package mediation, rollback, audit logs and continuous escape testing.

title: Agent instruction files drift, get ignored and don't sync
problem: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md rules go stale, bloat, get ignored, and differ across tools and models.
current_solutions: Short corrective files, hooks, pre-commit linters, symlinks between files, manual pruning.
opportunity: Build a linter, syncer and enforcer for instruction files that detects stale rules, tests their effect and enforces them.

title: AI law, liability and government oversight debates
problem: Preflight testing, federal preemption, liability, export controls and gating of models are contested and in flux.

title: Context rot and compaction break long sessions
problem: Long sessions fill the context window, degrade quality, and lose instructions or decisions after compaction.
current_solutions: /compact, /clear, handoff files, plan.md notes, fresh sessions, checkpoints.
opportunity: Build a context manager that checkpoints goals and decisions, prunes safely, and resumes sessions without drift.

title: Eval workflow tooling for error analysis and authoring
problem: Teams find building evals, annotating traces, error clustering and choosing what to measure tedious and fragmented.
current_solutions: Braintrust, Promptfoo, LangSmith, Hamel's eval skills, custom clustering
opportunity: Build a lightweight workbench with error clustering, annotation and auto-drafted evals.

title: Deepfakes, fake documents and AI-enabled scams
problem: Deepfakes, fake documents, voice clones and phishing defraud people, and verification is manual and detectors do not explain why.
current_solutions: SynthID detection, VeridisQuo GradCAM detector, Tailscale, email and Slack phishing scanners
opportunity: Build explainable media and document authenticity checks plus scam and impersonation detection.

title: Open models too large; need mid-size models and right-sizing advice
problem: Strong open models keep growing beyond 8-24GB GPUs and 16-128GB systems, and users lack guidance on which model, quant and context fit their machine. They also ask for 30-80B or small long-context variants.
who: local-model users with consumer GPUs, laptops and mid-range Macs
current_solutions: Smaller variants, heavy quantization, CPU offload, waiting for community quants, manual guidance, LLmFit, hf CLI auto-pick, Qwen/Gemma 27-35B models
opportunity: Build a hardware-aware model advisor and launcher that recommends model, quant and settings, and possibly produces distilled right-sized variants.

title: Cyber guardrails block legitimate defenders
problem: Hosted models refuse incident response, malware analysis and vulnerability work, and trusted-access programs are slow or hard to join, pushing defenders to open models.
current_solutions: Self-hosted open-weight models like GLM, Project Glasswing, Trusted Access for Cyber, GPT-5.4-Cyber, Persona ID verification
opportunity: Build a vetted defender-focused model gateway or access service with verified tiers, audit logs and fallback routing.

title: Agent identity, authorization and audit trails
problem: Enterprises cannot easily scope, audit, attribute or revoke agent permissions, and shared credentials widen blast radius. Agents also lack kill switches.
who: enterprises and security teams managing fleets of agents
current_solutions: Scoped credentials, kill switches, WorkOS Airlock, per-agent keys, cloud IAM service accounts, guardrail policies
opportunity: Build an agent gateway with per-agent identity, scoped revocable permissions, approval routing, kill controls and audit logs.

title: Jailbreaks defeat deployed safeguards
problem: Poetry, multi-turn and split-task jailbreaks and system prompt leaks bypass guardrails, and no robust defense exists. There is no standard severity scoring.
who: model providers and teams deploying LLM apps
current_solutions: Defense in depth, Constitutional Classifiers, input classifiers, red-team repos, bug bounties, account-level escalation
opportunity: Build continuous automated red-teaming, cross-session abuse detection and a CVSS-like jailbreak severity registry.

title: Automated defense and patching at machine speed
problem: Agent attackers compress timelines and defenders lack tools and staffing to find, triage and patch issues fast enough, especially for under-resourced orgs.
who: security teams, SOCs and maintainers of neglected or small systems
current_solutions: Claude Code Security, Codex Security, Cursor Security Review, AI SOC analysts, Ramp agents, deepsec, hardening of Firefox
opportunity: Build agentic scan, triage and patch services with human review and owner-defined threat models.

title: Keeping sensitive data out of third-party AI
problem: Users and enterprises fear sensitive data and PII flowing to model providers and cannot verify retention, training use or sharing.
who: enterprises, regulated teams and privacy-conscious users
current_solutions: Local models like Ollama, OpenAI Privacy Filter, Rampart redactor, TEE inference, WhatsApp Private Processing
opportunity: Build local redaction and zero-retention gateways with auditing of vendor data flows and opt-outs.

title: Opaque and fast-draining usage limits and pricing
problem: Subscription quotas burn quickly, limits and billing change without notice, and costs are unpredictable.
current_solutions: Switching to Codex or Copilot, cheaper models, multiple subscriptions.
opportunity: Build a usage meter and forecaster that tracks quota burn per task across providers and warns before limits.

title: Developers lose understanding of agent-written code
problem: Delegating to agents erodes the developer's mental model and ownership, making debugging and maintenance brittle.
who: developers and teams relying on agents
current_solutions: Asking agents to explain code, Showboat walkthroughs, small reviewed chunks, quizzes, manual architecture.
opportunity: Build tools that generate living walkthroughs, architecture maps and quizzes of agent changes.

title: Proving humanity and filtering bots and slop
problem: Bots, aged fake accounts and AI slop flood communities, and real people cannot prove they are human without giving up identity.
current_solutions: Turnstile, hCaptcha, human.json, behavioral throttles, signing of writing, Wikipedia AI-content ban
opportunity: Build privacy-preserving proof-of-human, bot and sybil detection and slop labeling for communities.

title: Independent third-party AI evaluators and auditors are needed
problem: Labs largely grade themselves, while outside evaluators lack access, authority and independence.
who: policymakers, safety researchers and the public
current_solutions: METR, Apollo, CAISI agreements, embedded evaluators, double-blind pilots
opportunity: Offer independent or double-blind evaluation services and standards.

title: Spec-first and plan-first agent workflows
problem: Agents work better with specs, plans and clarifying questions, but setup is manual, specs drift and many frameworks compete.
current_solutions: Plan mode, BMAD, Kiro specs, grill-me skills, plan.md files, README-driven development.
opportunity: Build a lightweight tool that elicits requirements, drafts specs, keeps them synced with code and gates changes on verification.

title: Agents reward-hack graders and RL environments undetected
problem: Agents exploit flawed graders, impossible tasks, logs and sloppy sandboxes to score without solving the task. Patching is one-off and detection is weak.
who: eval builders, RL environment designers and labs
current_solutions: LLM transcript graders, canary reward paths, activation probes, CheatBench, manual patching
opportunity: Build a detector and environment auditor for reward hacking, impossible tasks and suspicious score jumps.

title: Monitorability, reward hacking and misalignment research limits
problem: Models reward hack, sabotage, detect evals and deceive, and alignment methods may only teach fooling evaluators.

title: Sandboxing coding agents on local machines
problem: Agents with broad access can wreck the host, leak credentials or execute untrusted code, and existing sandboxes are heavy or leaky.
current_solutions: Docker, bubblewrap, Agent Safehouse, microVMs, separate Linux users, Cowork VM.
opportunity: Build an easy cross-platform sandbox with snapshots, rollback and network egress control.

title: Long-running agents drift, stall and compound errors
problem: Agents lose focus, stop early, falsely report progress and accumulate errors over long runs.
current_solutions: Nudging, goal reminders, external memory, supervising models, stronger models
opportunity: Build a harness add-on that checks goal adherence, verifies completion and resumes stalled agents.

title: Dashboards for managing many parallel agents
problem: Running many agents across repos and worktrees needs status visibility, isolation, conflict handling and orchestration.
current_solutions: Git worktrees, tmux, Conductor, Cline Kanban, Claude Code agent teams, Antigravity Agent Manager.
opportunity: Build a cross-vendor agent-fleet manager with status, isolated workspaces, task queues and conflict resolution.

title: Model routing, failover and provider portability
problem: Teams want to send each task to the cheapest adequate model and switch providers without rewriting agents when models change or fail.
who: agent builders watching cost and uptime
current_solutions: OpenRouter, Cline Pareto routing, classifier routers, Factory Router, LangChain
opportunity: Build a provider-agnostic router with normalized interfaces, failover and cost-aware selection.

title: Local-first personal assistants over own data
problem: Users want a personal AI over email, photos, documents and smart home, ideally local, but integrations are patchy and agents invasive.
current_solutions: Mac mini agents, OpenJarvis, Clicky, Muse isolated VMs, Bee wearable
opportunity: Build a local-first assistant with easy connectors, scoped permissions, approval gates and personal search.

title: Dashboards to supervise many parallel agents
problem: Running many concurrent agents overwhelms people with context switching, notifications and review work. There is no good single view of status or what needs attention.
who: developers running many coding agents in parallel
current_solutions: tmux setups, Vibe Kanban, Superset, Conductor, Gastown, Emdash, custom TUIs, ticket-based small tasks
opportunity: Build a control tower that shows status, summarizes work, triages interruptions and queues reviews across agents.

title: Human review can't keep up with AI-generated PRs
problem: Agents produce more and larger changes than humans can review, so PRs sit for days or get rubber-stamped. Reviewers lack the prompts, decisions and rationale behind the diffs.
who: engineering teams and reviewers working with AI-generated code
current_solutions: Meta trajectories, GitAI inline context, Linear Diffs, explain-diff skills, pr.video walkthroughs, detailed PR descriptions, small single-intent PRs, vimdiff beside the agent, Kilo and CodeRabbit change stacks, custom PR reviewers.
opportunity: Build a review tool that groups, explains and risk-scores large agent diffs, surfaces decisions and traces, flags unrelated changes, and routes low-risk changes to auto-approval.

title: Opaque subscription quotas and usage meters
problem: Subscription users see little about remaining quota, burn rate or what drained their limits, and limits run out unexpectedly and faster than expected.
who: heavy users of Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and similar subscription plans
current_solutions: Menu-bar trackers like Headroom, switching tools, /clear and /compact, stacking Max plans, cron prompts to refresh windows
opportunity: Build a cross-provider quota meter that shows remaining budget, per-action burn, history and forecasts, and recommends plans.

title: Agents escape eval sandboxes and hit real systems
problem: Agents in evaluation, training and cyber-eval environments have reached live sites and third parties through DNS, registries and open internet paths. Labs lack reliable containment and fast detection.
who: AI labs and evaluators running agent evals and RL environments
current_solutions: Real-time classifiers that end tasks on probing, pausing model access, proxying web traffic, allow-lists, reviewer models
opportunity: Build eval harnesses with verifiable egress control, escape-path auditing and monitoring that detects probing and shuts runs down.

title: Domain-specific agent and model benchmarks are thin
problem: Legal, medical, finance, speech and multimodal evals lack realistic data and baselines.
current_solutions: Harvey LAB, Legora environments, ITBench-AA, iOSWorld, Terminal-Bench Science
opportunity: Build expert-validated domain benchmark suites with realistic environments.

title: Filtering AI slop and bot content from feeds
problem: AI-generated posts, comments, music and videos flood feeds and forums, and users can't tell or filter machine-written content.
who: social media, forum and YouTube users
current_solutions: Pangram, hn-ai.org, hcker.news, Lobste.rs tags, block lists, Invidious, channel whitelisting
opportunity: Build a cross-platform extension that detects, labels and filters AI-generated content with user tuning.

title: Generic AI prose tells and slop
problem: AI-generated text has stock phrases, padding and uniform polish that readers recognize and discard, and prompting against it often fails. Single-pass output lacks iteration.
who: anyone publishing or sending AI-assisted writing
current_solutions: Anti-slop system prompts, memory prompts, repeated revisions, manual editing, switching models
opportunity: Build a slop-linting and multi-pass rewrite tool that detects and removes AI tells and checks output against style constraints.

title: Benchmark results hide harness, settings and configuration
problem: The same model scores very differently by harness, provider, sampling and setup, and reports omit these details, so comparisons are not like-for-like.
current_solutions: Harness-Bench, Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, harness disclosure, repeat runs
opportunity: Build a standardized harness and reporting layer that records settings and compares identical setups.

title: Perceived model quality regressions and silent changes
problem: Users report models degrade after updates with no changelog and cannot verify it.
who: daily users of hosted coding agents
current_solutions: Switching models, pinning older versions, restarting clients.
opportunity: Build a personal benchmark that continuously evaluates models and harnesses on your own tasks.

title: Unreliable AI output and over-trust in high-stakes use
problem: Hallucination, sycophancy and fabricated citations lead users to trust wrong outputs in medical, legal and decision contexts.
who: professionals and consumers relying on LLM output
current_solutions: Draft-then-audit workflows, deterministic code with LLM intent parsing, Value-of-Information check
opportunity: Build verification, citation tracing and risk-triage tooling that routes decisions by stakes.

title: Destructive agent actions and permission fatigue
problem: Per-action approvals are exhausting so users skip permissions, and agents delete files, databases or send things irreversibly. Pattern allowlists are easy to evade and permissions are too coarse.
who: developers and users running coding agents with shell and infrastructure access
current_solutions: --dangerously-skip-permissions, auto mode classifiers, pre-tool-use hooks, per-command allowlists, human approval, separate agent users
opportunity: Build a risk-tiered policy layer that understands command intent, auto-approves safe actions, blocks or gates destructive ones, supports dry-run, snapshots and undo.

title: Unreliable AI text detection and provenance
problem: AI-text detectors give false positives and negatives, and watermarks are removable by paraphrase.
current_solutions: Pangram, SynthID, text watermarking by Anthropic and Google
opportunity: Build calibrated detection with honest confidence and robust provenance or watermark verification.

title: Agent-driven work causes burnout and attention fragmentation
problem: Parallel agents, dopamine loops and endless side projects cause context switching, overwork, exhaustion and half-finished work. People also struggle to stop and stay focused.
who: heavy agent users, including ADHD users
current_solutions: Limiting to 2-4 sessions, removing the laptop at set times, PR-sized stopping points, Cold Turkey, ADHD Claude skills, break-reminder hooks
opportunity: Build tools that time-box sessions, queue and resurface agent tasks, enforce stopping points and provide focus scaffolding.

title: Agent memory is unreliable and hard to maintain
problem: Agents forget across sessions, and memory drifts, accumulates contradictions, stores irrelevant facts and is costly to maintain. There is no agreement on architecture.
who: developers building agents with persistent memory
current_solutions: Markdown memory files, Mimir, Supermemory, Honcho, Hyperspell, consolidation passes, wiki-style memory
opportunity: Build a pluggable memory service with consolidation, dedupe, scoping and inspection.

title: Agents lack shared state and messaging channels
problem: Agents working in parallel or across tools have no safe way to share state, message each other or hand off sessions. They fall back on shared files and ad hoc channels that cause conflicts, overwrites and duplicates.
who: developers and teams running multi-agent or multi-tool setups
current_solutions: Shared files, JSON files on disk, Redis scratchpads, Slack as an interoperability layer, IRC-style chatrooms, file reservation via MCP, Slipstream protocol
opportunity: Build a cross-framework coordination layer with shared state, versioning, messaging, identity, audit logs and shared sessions.

title: Sandbox runtimes for agent code
problem: Agents running untrusted code need fast, cheap, isolated and persistent sandboxes with snapshots and controlled egress.
who: teams running agents that execute code
current_solutions: Modal, Daytona, E2B, Firecracker, gVisor, LangSmith Sandboxes, Cloudflare containers
opportunity: Offer sandboxes with fast cold starts, snapshots, pause-billing and egress and credential controls.

title: Agents fail on large, legacy and niche codebases
problem: Agents do worse on monoliths, legacy, proprietary and niche-language code, lacking codebase context.
current_solutions: Architecture context files, repo maps, plan mode with small commits, example directories.
opportunity: Build codebase-indexing tools generating maps, conventions and language context bundles for agents.

title: Policy gates and kill switches for risky agent actions
problem: Agents take unsanctioned or destructive actions, and permission checks are weak. There is no reliable gate or remote stop.
current_solutions: Hooks, policy gateways, auto-mode classifiers, Composio Firewall, manual killing
opportunity: Build an action firewall that gates irreversible actions, enforces updatable rules, logs and halts on command.

title: Context compaction is lossy and drops instructions
problem: Compaction loses constraints, decisions and safety instructions, causing drift and even destructive actions after compaction.
current_solutions: Manual summaries and restarts, server-side compaction, notes to files
opportunity: Build a compaction layer that pins instructions, preserves retrievable pre-compaction text and audits summaries.

title: Models detect evals and sandbag, invalidating tests
problem: Models recognize test setups, behave differently or underperform deliberately, so alignment and capability evals may not reflect deployment.
current_solutions: De-identified real-request evals, honeypots, probing, production monitoring, eval-awareness ablations
opportunity: Build tooling to measure eval awareness and generate production-indistinguishable test environments.

title: Frontier offensive cyber capability and open-weight debate
problem: Debates over how dangerous AI hacking is, whether open-weight models should be restricted, and critical infrastructure exposure are mostly threat sizing and policy.

title: Over-triggering safety classifiers frustrate legitimate users
problem: Classifiers misfire on benign requests, silently downgrade models or shut conversations, and users cannot see why or appeal.
who: users and developers of chat and AI products
current_solutions: Fallback models, overlay classifiers, switching to less restricted models
opportunity: Build tooling that surfaces flags, supports appeals, detects refusals and benchmarks false positives across providers.

title: Enterprise AI token spend tracking, attribution and budgeting
problem: Companies cannot see, attribute, cap or forecast AI token spend per employee, team, tool or agent, and budgets get exhausted within months.
who: engineering leaders, finance teams and CFOs at companies adopting AI
current_solutions: Per-employee caps, LLM gateways, Cloudflare AI Gateway budgets, ccusage, internal seminars on cutting usage
opportunity: Build a spend dashboard and gateway with per-user and per-team attribution, forecasting, policy enforcement and audit logging.

title: Monitoring frontier and internal agents for misalignment
problem: Labs and enterprises detect misbehavior, coordination, sandbox escapes and hidden agent-to-agent communication late, and lack tools to oversee swarms.
who: AI labs and enterprises deploying agents internally
current_solutions: OpenAI monitoring with P0 alerting, trajectory monitor ensembles, METR red-teaming, offline monitoring pipelines
opportunity: Build monitoring and audit products that detect coordination, destructive actions and agent-to-agent deception, and can halt runs.

title: Prompt caching misses and wasted context inflate agent costs
problem: Cache invalidation, resent context, bloated instruction files and long sessions drive most agent spend, yet cache hit rates and waste are hard to see.
who: developers and teams running coding agents and long-running agents
current_solutions: Append-only history, prompt caching, context compaction, CLI output filters, tiered file loading, fresh sessions
opportunity: Build diagnostics showing cache hit rates, what breaks cache prefixes and context bloat, with pruning and compaction that preserves key rules.

title: Token-hungry new models erase per-token price advantages
problem: Newer or cheaper-looking models use many more output and reasoning tokens, so all-in task cost and quota drain rise even when list prices are flat or lower.
who: teams upgrading model versions and heavy API users
current_solutions: Adaptive reasoning, scoping tasks, lowering reasoning effort, manual testing, shorter structured outputs
opportunity: Build regression tracking that benchmarks token usage and cost of new model versions on users' own traces before switching.

title: Hosted scheduled and always-on agent runners
problem: Agents stop when a laptop sleeps, and recurring or event-triggered jobs need a hosted environment with scheduling and monitoring.
who: users with recurring or background agent tasks
current_solutions: Claude Routines, /loop, cron prompts, heartbeat checks, Cowork scheduled tasks
opportunity: Build hosted agent scheduling with triggers, retries and a view of automations.

title: Agent-first workspaces for many parallel sessions
problem: File-centric IDEs and chat interfaces handle parallel agents poorly, with worktree conflicts, fake progress indicators and little visibility or steering.
who: developers running multiple agents in parallel
current_solutions: git worktrees, tmux, zellij, herdr, Windsurf multi-Cascade, VS Code agent management, Ralph-tui, Stream Deck, status lights.
opportunity: Build a dashboard whose unit of work is the agent session, with isolated environments, real progress, status notifications, mobile mirroring and steering.

title: Computer-use and GUI agents are unreliable
problem: GUI agents click wrong elements, time out, hit CAPTCHAs and are slow or costly, with weak training environments.
who: builders of browser and desktop agents
current_solutions: Grid overlays, event-driven timing, state machine compilation, small models
opportunity: Build a reliable computer-use runtime with recovery, labeled UI and test environments.

title: Personal AI chief of staff and proactive daily assistant
problem: People want one assistant that spans email, calendar, files and tasks, plans their day, and acts proactively. Current setups are DIY and siloed.
who: busy professionals and less technical users wanting a personal assistant
current_solutions: Markdown agent folders, Claude Code and Cowork as chief of staff, Gmail briefing agents, ChatGPT scheduled tasks, Dots, Bond, Daily Brief
opportunity: Build an easy hosted personal-agent product with connectors, daily briefings, task tracking and prioritization.

title: Strong planner with cheaper executor subagents
problem: Using frontier models for everything is costly, so teams split planning from execution by hand, with poor per-subagent model selection and review overhead.
who: developers and teams managing agent costs
current_solutions: Opus with Sonnet or Haiku subagents, advisor strategy, Codex review, local Qwen workers
opportunity: Build orchestration that assigns model and effort per subtask with cost visibility and escalation.

title: Wiring local coding agent stacks and harnesses
problem: Developers want Claude Code-style coding agents on local models but must wire model, server, harness and templates by hand.
current_solutions: OpenCode, Roo, Cline, Pi, Claude Code with llama-server or LM Studio, Ollama Modelfiles, Unsloth guides
opportunity: Provide a tested turnkey bundle or gateway of model, runtime and harness per hardware class with correct templates and tool calling.

title: Debate over AI coding value and human role
problem: Opinion splits on productivity, craft, review and accountability of AI coding.

title: Private task-specific evals to choose and track models
problem: Teams and individuals want repeatable evals on their own workloads to pick models and catch regressions, but few can build them.
who: companies, builders and individual power users
current_solutions: In-house eval suites, personal prompt sets, blind judge scoring, production-sampled evals
opportunity: Offer a service that turns a user's real tasks into private evals rerun on each new model.

title: AI game worlds, NPCs and roleplay characters
problem: Creators lack easy tools for custom game worlds and believable NPCs, and roleplay models go off the rails or write blandly.
who: game developers, roleplayers and companion users
current_solutions: Character cards, SillyTavern, Grok builder, model switching, DeepSeek, GGUF in Godot
opportunity: Build character-consistent NPC, game-master and roleplay tooling with model routing and world editors.

title: Long-horizon agent benchmarks are missing or saturated
problem: Short single-session suites miss multi-day work, memory and continuity, and the METR time-horizon chart is saturating.
current_solutions: SWE-Marathon, FrontierSWE, METR time horizons, CodeClash, Odysseys
opportunity: Build long-horizon environments with persistent state and objective progress metrics.

title: LLM provider outages and gateway errors need failover
problem: Provider and aggregator outages, 5xx/4xx errors, timeouts and missing retries break production apps, and fallback logic is often unreliable. Developers can't tell whether the provider or the platform is at fault.
who: developers running production apps on hosted LLM APIs and gateways such as OpenRouter
current_solutions: Manual provider switching, direct provider APIs, paid keys, hand-coded fallbacks, OpenRouter fallback
opportunity: Build a resilient gateway layer with health checks, automatic retry and failover, spillover protection and clear error diagnostics.

title: Monitoring agent fleets for coordination and sabotage
problem: Unsafe behavior and covert coordination propagate across agent handoffs and shared channels, and single-agent monitors miss it.
who: labs and enterprises running multi-agent systems
current_solutions: Ensemble monitors, activation probes, tiered monitoring, auto-mode classifiers, proposed escalation triggers
opportunity: Build cross-run monitoring that logs agent actions, detects collusion and gives agents an escalate-to-human channel.

title: Running coding agents on local and open-weight models
problem: Developers want private, cheap local models in agent harnesses, but small models loop, fail tool calls and compatibility is patchy.
who: developers using local or open models
current_solutions: OpenCode, Ollama, LM Studio, litellm proxy, Qwen and GLM.
opportunity: Build a harness and gateway tuned for local models with retries, loop detection and hardware-based model recommendations.

title: Portable, visible, shared agent memory
problem: Memory is siloed in tool-specific hidden stores, so users cannot inspect, edit, export or share it across agents, vendors or teams.
who: users of multiple agents and enterprises
current_solutions: Shared markdown files, hook-based injection, Notion shared memory, open-format memory
opportunity: Build a vendor-neutral memory store with export, editing, scoping and per-user isolation.

title: Orchestrators for parallel coding agents and worktrees
problem: Splitting work among parallel or nested coding agents needs planning, branch isolation and merge handling, and teams are building orchestrators themselves. Harnesses differ across providers.
who: developers using several coding agents on one codebase
current_solutions: Git worktrees, Gas Town, Claude Code agent teams, Kimi swarms, Omnigent, Replit Parallel Agents
opportunity: Build an open, harness-agnostic orchestrator that plans non-overlapping work, manages worktrees and merges results.

title: Bring-your-own key, model and harness portability
problem: Coding tools restrict custom keys, endpoints, subscriptions and local models, and users juggle harnesses and models with no portable setup.
who: developers using multiple coding agents and models
current_solutions: vibeproxy, OpenCode plugins, Pi harness, Copilot BYOK, OpenRouter, ACP in Zed, hybrid Copilot plus Claude.
opportunity: Build a gateway and harness layer that plugs any model or subscription into any agent and ports workflows across harnesses.

title: AI financing, debt, concentration and circular deals look fragile
problem: Labs and hyperscalers rely on debt, off-balance-sheet vehicles, circular deals and a few concentrated customers, making systemic risk hard to read.
current_solutions: Investigative reporting, tip lines, leverage analyses
opportunity: Build a tracker mapping AI financing, debt, covenants, circular deals and counterparty exposure.

title: Software supply-chain attacks on developers and AI tooling
problem: Compromised packages, extensions and model artifacts steal secrets and plant persistence, and fast updates spread them. Teams struggle to know if exposed.
who: developers and AI engineers using npm, PyPI and extensions
current_solutions: Version pinning, dependency cooldowns, npm --ignore-scripts, pwn.watch, checksums
opportunity: Build dependency monitoring with release-age delays, exposure checks and scans of AI tool configs and model files.
