title: Running LLMs on old hardware, phones and edge devices
problem: People want models on CPUs, old phones, wearables and microcontrollers, but each setup needs custom builds, conversion and tuning.
current_solutions: llama.cpp on CPU and Termux, Google AI Edge Gallery, Bonsai, Cactus, Gemma E2B/E4B on MLX, kobold.cpp
opportunity: Provide an SDK and prebuilt runtimes with model bundles, conversion and benchmarks for common low-end devices and phones.

title: Confusing AI model lineups, modes and tool choice
problem: Fast-changing products with unclear names, modes and limits make it hard to know which model or tool to use, and users juggle several subscriptions side by side.
who: AI users and non-experts choosing between models and products
current_solutions: Running multiple frontier models side by side, manual copy-paste comparison, Inforno, OpenRouter, outside explainers
opportunity: Build a router and guide that recommends and compares models per task, tracks changes and consolidates subscriptions.

title: Simulated users and synthetic scenarios for agent testing
problem: Teams need many realistic scenarios and simulated users without production data, and multi-turn agent evals are fragile.
current_solutions: Arksim, Shopify SimGym, mock users, fault injection, user simulators
opportunity: Build a service generating synthetic users and scenarios from production traces.

title: Calibrating LLM judges against human labels
problem: Judges are rarely validated against human labels, and calibrating them is slow.
current_solutions: Binary per-dimension judges, TPR/TNR validation, train/dev/test labels
opportunity: Build a workflow that bootstraps and validates judges from few human labels.

title: Creators lack control over AI scraping and training use
problem: Creators cannot stop crawlers or find out when their work is used for training, and no-training licenses are hard to enforce.
who: creators, publishers and open source maintainers
current_solutions: robots.txt, Poison Fountain, Hippocratic License, modified MIT, AGPL
opportunity: Build scraper gating, training-use detection, opt-out and licensing tools.

title: Which coding model is best debates
problem: Users argue over which model or harness is best for coding.
current_solutions: Pairing Claude and Codex.

title: Cursor stability and account problems
problem: Cursor releases bring lag, memory leaks, crashes, lost chats, login loops, UI regressions and confusing token use.
current_solutions: Downgrading versions, shell script patches, deleting app data, switching tools.
opportunity: Offer a lighter, more stable agent IDE or a monitor that caps Cursor resource and token use.

title: Hard spend caps and budget gateways for LLM usage
problem: Provider spend limits are mostly soft alerts enforced after the fact, so teams get surprise bills. Teams need enforceable per-user, per-agent or per-period dollar and token caps.
who: teams and companies running LLM APIs and agents
current_solutions: AWS project spend limits, Google Cloud Spend Caps, Cloudflare AI Gateway budgets, thin proxies, virtual cards, manual watching
opportunity: Build a proxy or gateway that enforces real pre-request hard caps across providers, per team, user, agent or task.

title: Shared workspaces where humans and agents collaborate
problem: Agents work in isolation and sharing outputs or coordinating with people is lossy. Teams want agents inside shared threads, docs and the tools they already use.
who: teams working with multiple agents in Slack, Notion, Linear and shared documents
current_solutions: Slack-launched agents, Notion External Agents API, Linear agent workflows, Duet, Hubble, Poe group chat, kanban agent boards, Roughdraft markdown commenting
opportunity: Build a multiplayer workspace where people and agents share threads, documents, artifacts and handoffs.

title: Cache-aware routing and prompt caching for repeated prefixes
problem: Repeated long prefixes get recomputed because routing isn't cache-aware, prompt caching is manual and inconsistent across providers and gateways, and agent prompts bust prefixes.
who: teams serving or paying for agent and long-context workloads
current_solutions: NVIDIA Dynamo, vLLM Router, SGLang HiCache, LMCache, session-sticky routing, manual cache_control
opportunity: Build a caching and routing layer that keeps sticky prefix routing, detects prefix-busting content and reports cache hit rates across providers.

title: Tool design and tool-call failures
problem: Poorly designed tools and malformed tool calls across models and providers make agents unreliable and slow.
current_solutions: Outcome-oriented tool design, OpenRouter response healing, tool-call limits, rewritten descriptions
opportunity: Build a linter, validator and repair layer for tool definitions and calls.

title: AI slop eroding trust in search and online spaces
problem: Low-effort AI content crowds out human material and makes authorship hard to judge, and backlash against AI media grows.
current_solutions: Unfollowing, small communities, disclosure labels
opportunity: Build provenance and curation tools that surface human-authored and disclosed material.

title: Personal knowledge bases and second brains for agents
problem: People want years of notes, bookmarks, emails and files organized and searchable by LLMs and agents. Ad hoc setups for sync, structure and local search are fragile.
who: knowledge workers, researchers and note-takers using Obsidian or markdown vaults with agents
current_solutions: Obsidian with Claude Code, Karpathy-style markdown wikis, custom MCP servers, SyncThing and git hooks, SQLite FTS5 indexers, local Qwen search, QMD playbooks, Notion workers
opportunity: Build a packaged, local-first, agent-ready personal knowledge vault that ingests notes, bookmarks, emails and files and supports plain-English search and sync.

title: Running huge MoE models on consumer hardware
problem: Frontier open MoE models far exceed consumer VRAM and RAM, and users must tune offload and SSD streaming by hand, with CUDA-only or incomplete support.
who: local LLM enthusiasts wanting large open models
current_solutions: Flash-MoE SSD streaming, DwarfStar, llama.cpp offload flags, hot-expert caching, AirLLM, 2-bit quantization, Krasis
opportunity: Build a runtime that auto-tiers weights and experts across VRAM, RAM and SSD and reports realistic speeds.

title: Quantization quality is poorly measured and breaks agents
problem: Quant comparisons use perplexity or throughput only, labels are inconsistent, and low-bit quants break tool calling, loop or degrade unpredictably. Users cannot tell which quant is safe for their task.
who: local-model users choosing GGUF and other quants
current_solutions: KL-divergence comparisons, Unsloth dynamic GGUFs, imatrix pipelines, QAT, higher-bit quants, trial and error, Hugging Face hardware filters
opportunity: Build a quant benchmark and registry service publishing KLD and real task metrics, especially tool calling, per quant and hardware.

title: AI thinking partners that push back
problem: Chatbots flatter and agree, so users want AI that challenges assumptions, offers perspectives and raises ambition. Many also don't know how to prompt for real judgment.
who: people using AI to brainstorm and evaluate ideas
current_solutions: Adversarial custom instructions, steelmanning, persona debates, Absolute Mode prompts, devil's advocate requests, meta-prompting
opportunity: Build a thought-partner app with critic modes and multiple perspectives that draws on the user's past work and shows its verification.

title: Open source maintainers flooded with AI slop
problem: Maintainers receive growing volumes of low-quality AI-generated PRs, issues and security reports that cost more to triage than they are worth. There are no reliable trust signals.
current_solutions: Manual profile inspection, closing external PRs, Vouch contributor vetting, Pangram or Claude prefiltering, review bots, blocking new users, Linux kernel AI guidelines.
opportunity: Build a triage and reputation layer that scores, filters and verifies incoming PRs and reports for quality, reproducibility and AI provenance.

title: Agent tracing, trace storage and viewers
problem: Agent behavior is decided at runtime, so traces are the main debugging artifact, but they need good storage, ingestion, viewing and replay.
who: teams building and operating LLM agents
current_solutions: LangSmith, Langfuse, Arize Phoenix, Datadog LLM Observability, OpenTelemetry, SmithDB, Raindrop, custom trace viewers
opportunity: Build lightweight open tracing with fast ingestion, deduplicated history, nested trace viewing and replay.

title: Efficient attention and architecture research
problem: Researchers explore sparse, linear, hybrid, looped and latent-reasoning architectures to cut cost, with disputed evidence on what matters.
current_solutions: Gated DeltaNet; sliding window attention; DeepSeek mHC; looped transformers; Coconut; diffusion LLMs

title: Safety and dangerous-capability evals are saturated, narrow and costly
problem: Safety, bio and cyber evals saturate quickly, probe only predefined failure paths, and are slow and expensive to run. Risk thresholds are vague.
current_solutions: Headroom eval suites, production evals on live traffic, triage of evaluations, proposed shared cross-lab metrics
opportunity: Build shared, cheaper, frontier-calibrated safety eval suites with rare-behavior estimation.

title: Agent identity and scoped delegated permissions
problem: Agents inherit users' full permissions, with no standard for identity, delegation or least-privilege access, which exposes them to injection and leaks.
current_solutions: WorkOS Airlock, Windows agent identities, namespaced profiles, trusted-model restrictions
opportunity: Offer scoped delegated credentials, RBAC and audit trails per agent.

title: Private offline and local voice assistants
problem: Users want dictation, TTS and assistants that run locally without cloud data or costs, with configurable models and tool calling.
who: privacy-minded users, accessibility users and developers
current_solutions: Hex, WisprFlow, Kokoro, Spokenly with Parakeet, CODEC, AnythingLLM, Samsung Hey Plex
opportunity: Build polished local dictation, TTS and voice assistant apps with custom LLM endpoints and system control.

title: Uncontrolled AI token spend and budgeting
problem: Inference costs per engineer and tool are rising and hard to budget, so companies ration usage, cap spend or cut access without clear ROI.
current_solutions: Uber per-tool cap; role-based tiering; routing to cheaper models (Coinbase, AT&T, Lindy on DeepSeek); Shopify DSPy optimization
opportunity: Build spend-governance software that tracks tokens per team, sets budgets with chargeback, and routes tasks to the cheapest adequate model.

title: Speculative decoding is fragmented and hard to tune
problem: MTP, EAGLE-3, DFlash, DSpark and n-gram methods give speedups in some setups and slowdowns in others, with buggy or incomplete llama.cpp support and little guidance or fair benchmarks.
who: local and server LLM users wanting faster generation
current_solutions: MTP in llama-server, Luce DFlash, vLLM DSpark, ik_llama.cpp, GGUF surgery scripts, manual flag tuning
opportunity: Build a tool that auto-selects and tunes speculative method, draft model and MTP-enabled GGUFs, benchmarking real gains per model and hardware.

title: Subsidized AI pricing makes economics fragile and prices uncertain
problem: Flat-rate plans and AI startups lean on subsidized inference and VC cash, so users and builders fear price hikes and burn spikes when subsidies end. Whether prices will rise or fall is contested.
who: AI startups, builders and heavy subscription users
current_solutions: Passing price increases to customers, fundraising, cheaper or open models, diversifying providers
opportunity: Build cost-scenario modeling and multi-provider abstraction tooling that stress-tests burn against API price changes.

title: Runtime watchdogs and guardrails for autonomous agents
problem: Agents have gone unmonitored for weeks, leaked data, deleted repos, coordinated exploits or disabled monitors, and offline review is too slow.
who: labs and enterprises running agent fleets
current_solutions: Watcher Live, MCPShark, watchdog agents, OpenAI multistage monitoring, auto-review systems, 24/7 CoT monitoring
opportunity: Build a runtime monitor that detects anomalies, blocks actions, pauses sessions and resists being disabled.

title: Identity, permissions and access control for enterprise agents
problem: Enterprises lack per-agent identity, scoped credentials and permission-aware access to company data and APIs. Agents are often trusted by default and shared identities conflict with audit logs.
who: enterprise IT and security teams deploying agents
current_solutions: Cloudflare AI Gateway; MCP servers with SSO/OAuth; Descope IAM for agents; enterprise-managed MCP auth; banks treating agents as managed digital employees
opportunity: Build an agent identity and authorization control plane with scoped credentials, least-privilege data access, audit logs and approvals.

title: Unpredictable AI vendor price, plan and model-access changes
problem: Vendors raise, cut and restructure prices and plans, remove model access and deprecate models with little notice, often through quiet page edits. Builders cannot plan around them.
who: app builders and users depending on AI vendor plans and models
current_solutions: Switching providers, open models, OpenRouter, manual monitoring
opportunity: Build a monitor that tracks vendor pricing pages, terms, model availability and sunset dates and alerts users to changes with cost-impact forecasts and migration help.

title: Small fine-tuned specialists replacing frontier models
problem: Frontier models are costly and slow on narrow, repeated tasks, and fine-tuned or distilled small models can match them. Teams lack the expertise to build them, and custom models may be superseded by newer bases.
who: companies running high-volume narrow tasks on frontier APIs
current_solutions: Shopify and Liquid AI distillation, Harvey fine-tuned Kimi, Cursor Composer, Databricks KARL, ModernBERT classifiers, routers
opportunity: Offer a pipeline that turns usage traces and a benchmark into a cheaper specialist model, routes between models, and ports fine-tunes to new bases.

title: Specs and delegation briefs before agent runs
problem: Underspecified goals waste agent hours, and users need help writing specs, success criteria and plans and breaking work into reviewable tasks.
who: people delegating long or large tasks
current_solutions: Plan mode, plan.md, spec.md milestones, interview prompts, ticket loops
opportunity: Build a spec authoring tool that elicits context, defines done states and decomposes work.

title: AI bubble and sustainability debate
problem: Commentators disagree on whether AI spending and valuations are a bubble and what a correction would look like.
current_solutions: Holding cash, gold or treasuries

title: Agents claim success without end-to-end verification
problem: Agents say work is verified without proof, and developers lack evidence such as screenshots and live-app runs, especially for UI.
current_solutions: Playwright, screenshot diffs, recorded test videos, curl exercises
opportunity: Build agent-driven QA that runs the full stack and records pass/fail evidence.

title: Inboxes, phones, payments and identity for agents
problem: Agents lack ways to receive messages, call, pay or register for services safely.
current_solutions: Twilio, one-time virtual cards, auth.md, here.now
opportunity: Provide agent-ready inbox, phone, card and storage primitives with abuse controls.

title: Production observability and ops for AI-generated code
problem: AI-accelerated shipping raises on-call burden, and AI code ignores instrumentation conventions. Teams need agent-friendly logs, incident context and production validation.
who: engineering and SRE teams shipping AI-generated code
current_solutions: Sazabi, Interfere, AI SRE startups, Datadog MCP, CLI-accessible logs, canaries, auto-rollbacks
opportunity: Build agent-ready incident tooling linking code, runtime state and runbooks that validates AI changes in production and rolls back safely.

title: Measuring real AI productivity gains
problem: People overestimate gains, usage and output metrics mislead, and it's hard to tell when AI helps or wastes time. Teams lack outcome-level measures.
who: individuals, team leads and executives adopting AI
current_solutions: Comparing to prior estimates, session and context-switch tracking, Epoch-style tracking
opportunity: Build analytics that measure outcomes such as shipped PRs and closed tickets and advise when delegating to AI pays off.

title: Personal vibe-coded tools and sharing them
problem: People build bespoke small apps but struggle to debug, harden, distribute or showcase them.
current_solutions: Claude, Gemini AI Studio, Wabi, Grok hosted pages
opportunity: Build a platform to create, harden, share and showcase micro-apps.

title: Multi-model chat front ends with better UX and file handling
problem: Official chat apps have weak mobile clients, upload limits, truncated documents and missing features. Users want many models in one place.
current_solutions: Kagi Assistant, Perplexica, OpenRouter front ends, OkeyBot, Inforno, Gemini full-file ingestion
opportunity: Build a polished BYO-key multi-model client with large-file handling, cost tracking and comparison.

title: Military and government use of frontier AI
problem: Vendors cannot enforce usage limits on classified or military deployments and legal frameworks are lacking.
current_solutions: Contract redlines, vendor safety stacks

title: Reasoning models overthink, wasting tokens, context and time
problem: Reasoning models produce long traces on trivial prompts, fill context and run slowly, and disabling thinking is inconsistent across models.
who: local and API users of reasoning models
current_solutions: no_think flags, template changes, logit bias on 'wait', system prompt caps, instruct variants, effort levels
opportunity: Build middleware that sets reasoning effort per request and trims thinking tokens across local runtimes.

title: Silent degradation of hosted models goes untracked
problem: Hosted models may be nerfed, quantized or rerouted, and users lack a standard way to detect regressions.
who: developers and teams relying on hosted models
current_solutions: Anecdotes, ad hoc retesting, mirrored production traffic, LiveNerf frozen panels
opportunity: Run a scheduled fixed-panel tracker on providers that charts drift and alerts.

title: Token waste from tools, search and verbose loops
problem: Agents burn tokens on naive grep, loaded tool definitions, retries and rediscovering codebase structure.
current_solutions: Semantic search tools (osgrep, mgrep), code graphs, DeepWiki MCP, disabling tools, caching.
opportunity: Build token-efficient code search, code-graph and tool-loading middleware plus token profilers.

title: Triaging agent failures from traces into evals
problem: Agent failures are reasoning failures across long traces and nobody can read them all, so teams need clustering, root-cause classification and conversion into evals.
current_solutions: Langfuse, promptfoo, LangSmith Engine, Raindrop Triage, W&B Weave, Sazabi, trace sampling
opportunity: Build a trace triage tool that clusters failures, classifies root causes and feeds annotations into regression evals.

title: KV cache memory limits long-context inference
problem: KV cache memory limits context length and concurrency, and compression or quantization methods vary in real speed, quality and support.
who: operators of long-context and agent workloads on server and consumer GPUs
current_solutions: TurboQuant, KVarN, RotorQuant, DMS, MLA, FP8 KV, CPU offload, sparse attention
opportunity: Ship a drop-in KV compression and offload library with verified speed, memory and accuracy benchmarks across engines.

title: Frontier model access cut off by governments or vendors
problem: Export controls, staged government-approved releases and vendor decisions abruptly restrict or delay frontier model access. Products and workflows break with little warning.
who: enterprises and downstream product builders relying on frontier models
current_solutions: Multi-vendor hedging; backup contracts with non-US vendors; requesting special API access; Microsoft keeping Anthropic available
opportunity: Build a resilient access layer with automatic failover and availability monitoring.

title: Agents misread intent, overreach and skip clarifying questions
problem: Agents make confident wrong assumptions, change more than asked and need constant steering.
current_solutions: Explicit prompts, ask-before-assuming rules, interview prompts, AGENTS.md bans.
opportunity: Build a pre-task clarification and scope guard that surfaces assumptions and constrains edits to the requested region.

title: Frontier models cost too much; need routing and price comparison
problem: Buyers pay a premium for top models that few tasks need, and per-token comparisons mislead because token usage and bundles vary. Teams lack an easy way to pick the cheapest adequate model per task and track cost.
who: developers and teams using multiple model APIs and coding agents
current_solutions: Cheaper models (Sonnet, Flash, DeepSeek), open-weight models, OpenRouter, manual switching, ad-hoc benchmarking
opportunity: Build a router and benchmark dashboard that measures cost per completed task, sends each prompt to the best-value model and tracks per-model spend.

title: Autonomous research and experiment agents
problem: Researchers want multi-agent pipelines and experiment loops, but pruning ideas, verification and scaling remain hard.
current_solutions: Sakana Agentic Scientist, Kosmos, Karpathy loop, autoresearch
opportunity: Offer research-agent templates with benchmarks, experiment tracking and verification.

title: Coding agent and enterprise token spend gets expensive and untracked
problem: Developers and companies burn tokens quickly with surprise bills and variable billing, and cannot link spend to output. Integrations can burn thousands of credits in seconds with no guardrails.
who: developers running coding agents and engineering orgs managing token budgets
current_solutions: Flat plans, spending caps, cheaper models, Ramp's spend tracking, expensing subscriptions
opportunity: Build a spend monitor with caps, per-task credit limits, model routing and spend-to-outcome analytics for teams.

title: Silent model swapping and unclear model or effort level
problem: Providers silently route to weaker models, effort toggles seem to do nothing, and users cannot see which model answered.
current_solutions: Manually selecting models, custom instructions, switching providers
opportunity: Build a transparency tool showing which model and effort actually ran, with per-task recommendations.

title: Chain-of-thought monitorability is eroding
problem: Reasoning traces are getting less legible or trained against, weakening a key oversight method.
current_solutions: CoT and action monitors, activation monitoring, interpretability
opportunity: Build independent services that benchmark monitorability, possibly interpretability-based.

title: Fine-tuning causes unintended side effects and misalignment
problem: Narrow or bad fine-tuning data causes emergent misalignment, persona drift and hidden behaviors that are hard to detect or undo.
who: teams fine-tuning models and safety researchers
current_solutions: Inoculation prompting, SAE diffing, deception probes, introspection adapters, checkpoint reverts
opportunity: Build behavior-diff and regression tools that scan models before and after fine-tuning for side effects.

title: Verifying agent work with independent reviewers
problem: Agents claim work is done when it is not, fabricate results and agree sycophantically, so independent verification is needed.
current_solutions: Reviewer agents, cross-model review, adversarial checkers, deterministic checks
opportunity: Package a reusable critic and verification pipeline checking work against the spec.

title: AI slide and office document generation
problem: Generated slides and documents are image-based, hard to edit, mangle formatting and look generic. Slide tools are clumsy for technical content.
who: professionals and builders producing decks and documents
current_solutions: Gamma, NotebookLM slides, Perplexity asset creation, Claude Office files, Kami design skill, Julius, Paper2Slides, Keynote WebP export
opportunity: Build an agent-native deck and document tool with editable HTML or PDF output, preserved formatting, varied layouts, charts and citations.

title: Prompt injection, secrets leakage and supply-chain risk for agents
problem: Untrusted content, packages and harnesses can hijack agents or exfiltrate code, keys and data through allowed channels.
current_solutions: Hooks, scoped tokens, domain allowlists, classifiers, credential proxies.
opportunity: Build scanners, egress monitors and credential brokers that vet inputs and installs.

title: Fine-tuning and distilling open models for enterprise tasks
problem: Companies want small proprietary models fine-tuned or distilled from frontier models for repetitive tasks, but the process is hand-built and uncertain.
current_solutions: Fine-tuned small Qwen3, distillation to sub-8B students, replay-based migration, Unsloth, MLX fine-tuning, LoRA adapters
opportunity: Offer fine-tuning and distillation as a service or local toolkit that converts traces into small models with cost-quality comparison and LoRA export.

title: Estimating and bounding cost of agentic workflows
problem: One user action triggers many calls via tools, retries, subagents and reasoning, so cost is hard to forecast and spikes only appear with real users.
current_solutions: Per-step cost tracking, separating retries and heavy paths, scoped tasks
opportunity: Build a cost-modeling tool that forecasts workflow cost from step composition and flags runaway paths.

title: Coding agents lack persistent cross-session memory
problem: Agents forget preferences, decisions and mistakes between sessions, so users hand-maintain notes and memory files.
who: developers using agents across many sessions
current_solutions: Claude-Mem, MEMORY.md files, Cline memory bank, git-tracked context repos, Letta Code.
opportunity: Offer a provider-independent memory layer that stores, prunes and re-injects project knowledge.

title: Deciding what to build when building is cheap
problem: Shipping is cheap, so deciding what should exist, proving impact, and linking customer feedback to prototypes are the bottleneck. Review and testing lag behind fast coding.
current_solutions: Pilot-scale-kill cycles, prototype-first handoffs, feedback-driven idea generation, dogfooding
opportunity: Build tools that ground ideas in customer feedback, track feature value and speed review and handoffs.

title: Local LLM apps (LM Studio, Ollama, KoboldCPP) are buggy
problem: Local runtimes crash, leak state, have small default contexts, non-portable installs, stale llama.cpp and missing features, often failing silently.
current_solutions: Manual context increases, using llama.cpp directly, switching runtimes, lightweight GUIs, Fox
opportunity: Build a more reliable local server and GUI with sane defaults, current llama.cpp, portable install and diagnostics.

title: Documentation and APIs made consumable by agents
problem: Docs drift from code and agents need current, machine-readable docs, CLIs and version lists, but many libraries lack them.
current_solutions: Mintlify Autopilot and llms.txt, Context7 CLI, context-hub, DeepWiki, AGENTS.md, docs as npm packages.
opportunity: Build a service that keeps agent-ready docs and current-version indexes updated from code, with quality feedback.

title: Soft qualities and non-verifiable tasks lack benchmarks
problem: Writing, empathy, taste and open-ended research have no cheap objective judge, and AI judges favor AI writing.
current_solutions: EQBench, human rater rubrics, LLM judges
opportunity: Build reproducible evals and rubric-grading tools for subjective traits.

title: Private local transcription, dictation and meeting capture
problem: Users want fast private transcription of speech, long recordings and meetings, voice dictation into any app, and meeting follow-ups or coaching without cloud bots.
current_solutions: MacWhisper, Parakeet, Spokenly, Wispr Flow, Typeless, Granola Briefs, Radiant, Alter
opportunity: Build a local-first voice and meeting app with speaker labels, direct text insertion, summaries, tasks and coaching that agents can call.

title: Secure fast sandboxes for AI agents
problem: Agents running untrusted code need fast-starting isolated environments with snapshots and persistent state, while weak isolation and exposed endpoints allow escapes and secret theft.
who: teams running agents, RL and evals
current_solutions: Firecracker microVMs, Modal snapshots, Koyeb and Cloudflare sandboxes, Sprites, DeepSeek DSec
opportunity: Build a managed or self-hostable sandbox service with microVM isolation, egress controls, fast snapshot restore and resizing.

title: Visual feedback loops between UI and coding agents
problem: Developers want to point at UI elements, show bugs and give agents visual and browser feedback, but passing images and context is manual.
current_solutions: CSS Studio, Agentation, React Grab, DOM pickers, Chrome DevTools MCP, Scrawl, screen recordings.
opportunity: Build a tool that annotates live UI, captures screenshots, voice and DOM state, and sends precise context to agents.

title: Chat is a high-friction interface; generative UIs
problem: Chat is awkward for shopping, travel and recurring tasks, and users want task-specific or generated interfaces.
current_solutions: Generative UI projects, Gemini Dynamic View, OpenUI
opportunity: Build generative-UI layers that replace chat for recurring workflows with user control.

title: Deterministic validators and workflow graphs around LLMs
problem: Models do not reliably follow prompt rules, and fully agentic flows deviate, so teams want deterministic code to control and validate LLM steps.
current_solutions: Blueprints, DAG planners, validators plus human approval, state machines
opportunity: Build a framework mixing deterministic nodes and LLM nodes with verifier gates.

title: Automating ML experiment loops and autonomous research agents
problem: Running ideas to results is slow and manual, and setting up agent experiment loops is bespoke. Full AI scientist agents struggle with open-ended tasks and need human verification.
who: ML researchers and labs running agentic research
current_solutions: Karpathy's autoresearch; Claude experiment loops; agent swarms; Hyperagents; AI Scientist; Recursive; Google ERA; Hugging Face ml-intern
opportunity: Build an open orchestration harness for experiment sweeps, tracking, validation and reproducibility with human-in-the-loop checks.

title: Hidden model reasoning and silent behavior changes
problem: Hidden thinking output, undocumented harness changes, silent model fallbacks and opaque prompts leave users unable to see what the model did or why behavior changed.
who: heavy users and auditors of coding agents
current_solutions: Pinning older Claude Code versions, thinking-summary flags, proxy interception, stderr reasoning display, change records.
opportunity: Build an observability layer that captures reasoning, prompts and tool use and flags version changes and silent fallbacks.

title: Managed fine-tuning services for open models
problem: Fine-tuning or RL-tuning open models still needs GPUs, expert engineering and architecture-specific serving decisions, especially after frontier-lab fine-tuning APIs were withdrawn.
who: enterprises and non-expert teams customizing open models
current_solutions: Tinker, Fireworks, Prime Intellect Lab, Mistral Forge, Unsloth notebooks, Hugging Face skills
opportunity: Build a managed, self-serve service that handles data prep, training, evaluation and serving for open models.

title: GPU kernel programming is hard and error-prone
problem: Writing kernels in CUDA, CuTe, Triton and Mojo hits bank conflicts, numerics bugs, silent correctness failures, poor docs and clumsy benchmarking, and timing harnesses mislead.
who: GPU kernel authors and inference engineers
current_solutions: Helion autotuning, CuTeDSL, cuTile, Nsight profiling, popcorn-cli, Hugging Face Kernels
opportunity: Build kernel authoring, debugging and testing tools that check outputs against references, flag silent divergence and give trustworthy benchmarks.

title: Reliable spreadsheet, BI and financial analyst agents
problem: Agents in Excel and Sheets are slow, fragile and error-prone, quality varies by vendor, and analysts want checkable models and actionable BI. Office integrations from Google and Microsoft underperform Claude.
who: analysts and teams working in Excel, Sheets and Office
current_solutions: Claude for Excel, ChatGPT in Excel/Sheets, Shortcut, Sheets Canvas, Interpreter, Crunched, Claude Cowork, Workspace Studio
opportunity: Build a cross-suite Office and spreadsheet agent that shows assumptions, verifies work and handles mixed files and bulk edits.

title: Public opposition and risk discourse
problem: Backlash, disputed risk messaging and environmental critiques shape debate.

title: Saturated public benchmarks need harder replacements
problem: Major benchmarks are maxed out, noisy or answerable without reading the question, so they no longer separate frontier models. Good unsaturated evals are scarce.
who: labs, model buyers and benchmark maintainers
current_solutions: Moving-target benchmarks like Frontier-Bench, harder ARC-AGI versions, SatBench saturation tracking, harder tiers
opportunity: Build continuously refreshed, hard-to-saturate benchmark suites and a tracker that flags saturation and curates replacements.

title: Agent framework churn and build-versus-buy
problem: Frameworks change fast, break between releases and are often seen as overengineered, so teams roll their own.
current_solutions: LangGraph, Mastra, OpenAI Agents SDK, Strands, DeepAgents, minimal custom harnesses

title: Benchmarks of real economic work and productivity
problem: Scores do not map to completed work, dollar outcomes or labor cost, and productivity studies are untrustworthy.
current_solutions: GDPval, Vending-Bench, AA-Briefcase
opportunity: Build independent real-work benchmarks measuring outcomes by domain.

title: Pelican-style informal benchmarks need comparison tooling
problem: Informal SVG and creative prompts are used as personal benchmarks but are hard to compare across models and effort levels, and are losing signal.
current_solutions: llm CLI, comparison grids, render-and-iterate loops, secret backup prompts
opportunity: Build a gallery that runs fixed visual prompts across models and effort levels with grading and cost tallies.

title: RL training frameworks, throughput and systems bottlenecks
problem: LLM RL training is slow and complex because of weight sync, rollout cost, train-inference mismatch and synchronous updates. Choosing a framework is confusing.
current_solutions: TRL AsyncGRPO, Miles, SLIME, VeRL, SkyRL, Axolotl, bitwise-consistent TRL+vLLM, speculative decoding in rollouts, async RL
opportunity: Offer a lightweight, fast RL framework or hosted service with async rollouts, fast weight sync and benchmarked defaults.

title: Verifying AI-generated code beyond line-by-line review
problem: Generated code volume outpaces human review, and agents misreport what they did.
current_solutions: Holdout scenario tests, Antithesis, linters, per-PR environments, sampled human review
opportunity: Build verification tooling that checks agent output and claims independently.

title: Self-improving harnesses with safe rollback
problem: Automated harness optimization gives unstable gains and can silently break behavior, so changes need evals and rollback.
current_solutions: Autoagent, Darwin Gödel Machine, LangChain hill-climbing, nightly AGENTS.md updates
opportunity: Build tooling tracing harness changes, gating them with held-out evals and enabling rollback.

title: Agents need company context and tacit knowledge
problem: Business rules and tacit knowledge live in meetings, emails and scattered systems that agents cannot see, so agents lack governed company context.
current_solutions: Airbnb Everest context graph; hybrid RAG over internal docs; MCP servers for Slack/Drive; Glean; WorkOS Atlas; HubSpot HubCode
opportunity: Build a permission-aware organizational memory and context layer that captures meetings and procedures and connects company data for agents.

title: Publishing and deploying agent-built apps without friction
problem: Shipping requires signing, compliance, accounts, DNS, OAuth and infrastructure steps that agents and beginners struggle with.
who: builders of AI-generated sites and apps
current_solutions: here.now, Cloudflare Drop and temporary deploys, GitHub Pages, Fastlane, gistpreview, Dokku.
opportunity: Build zero-account instant deploy and publishing that handles signing, compliance and hosting.

title: Chatbot pushback, over-caution and over-censorship
problem: Assistants argue, lecture, refuse harmless or creative requests, and block benign prompts. Users reframe or jailbreak to get answers.
who: chatbot users doing creative, bureaucratic or everyday tasks
current_solutions: Prompt reframing, jailbroken Gemini, switching models, incognito mode, DeepSeek, RawChat stealth mode
opportunity: Build a wrapper with user-controlled behavior, refusal explanations, fewer false refusals and adjustable content settings.

title: LLM APIs and client libraries are fragmented and fast-changing
problem: Provider APIs and settings diverge, reasoning controls differ, and libraries lag behind new model features, making integration and comparison hard.
current_solutions: LLM CLI plugins, Open Responses spec, OpenRouter, custom adapters, migration guides.
opportunity: Build a conformance and abstraction layer that normalizes settings, tests provider capabilities and pins versions.

title: Chat service outages, lost history and billing failures
problem: Chat services go down, rate-limit, drop messages and history, and have payment errors and slow support.
current_solutions: Alternative assistants, restarting the app, emailing support
opportunity: Build a multi-provider client with failover, quota tracking and chat backup/export.

title: Local inference cost versus hosted APIs and hedging
problem: Buyers debate whether local rigs beat hosted APIs, while others self-host to hedge API price hikes, deprecation and silent changes.
who: individuals and companies weighing local hardware
current_solutions: Mac Studio and 3090 rigs, DGX Spark clusters, Qwen via Ollama, local archiving of weights
opportunity: Build cost calculators, migration tooling and managed local or on-prem setups with version pinning.

title: Distillation toolkits and teacher-trace curation
problem: Distillation into smaller models gives inconsistent results, can import teacher quirks or mismatched planning, and needs heavy curation of traces. Methods are scattered.
who: teams distilling frontier or reasoning models into small ones
current_solutions: MOPD, on-policy distillation, trace distillation from Claude or GLM, thinking-token masking, DPO with strong-vs-weak pairs, Upskill
opportunity: Build a toolkit that collects, scores and filters teacher traces and tests whether distillation helps the student.

title: Human approval, escalation and pause/resume
problem: Agents need to pause for human approval, resume later and escalate ambiguous cases without causing approval fatigue.
who: teams running agents with side effects
current_solutions: Human routing tools, Dial MCP, confidence-based routing, ask_clarification tools
opportunity: Build a risk-tiered approval service with resumable tool calls and multi-channel escalation.

title: Mandated AI usage and token leaderboards get gamed
problem: Forced AI usage metrics, token leaderboards and review requirements push employees to game numbers, producing low-value use, resentment and waste.
who: employees and managers under AI mandates
current_solutions: Employee petitions; defining outcomes and letting engineers choose tools; some teams banning agentic dev
opportunity: Build usage analytics that tie AI consumption to useful outcomes by workflow rather than raw activity.

title: Frontier models too slow for flow and agent loops
problem: Top models and tool calls are slow, fast modes carry steep premiums, and tokens per second ignores tool time and time-to-first-token. Slowness breaks flow and compounds across agent steps.
who: developers running coding agents and production AI apps
current_solutions: Opus fast mode, highspeed tiers, Codex-Spark, Cerebras, routing subagents to fast models, hybrid local/API
opportunity: Build end-to-end latency benchmarking and budgeting tools that mix fast and slow models.

title: AI-driven vulnerability discovery and triage
problem: Agents find zero-days quickly, so defenders need equivalent scanning and triage.
current_solutions: Mythos Preview, Project Glasswing, Devin Security, Claude Code Security.
opportunity: Offer repeatable find, patch and prove-with-test vulnerability pipelines with reachability checks.

title: Python environment, packaging and distribution friction
problem: Python versions, locking, breaking tool upgrades, missing wheels and shipping compiled code to PyPI or Pyodide remain painful, though uv helps.
current_solutions: uv, uvx, dependency groups, go-to-wheel, cibuildwheel for Pyodide, Justfile recipes.
opportunity: Build helpers that package native code into multi-platform wheels and Pyodide targets and check compatibility and upgrades.

title: Automated and cross-model AI code review
problem: Teams want an independent AI reviewer that catches what the authoring model missed, but built-in review is costly, noisy and shallow.
who: teams using coding agents and CI
current_solutions: Custom headless reviewers in CI, Codex reviewing Claude (and vice versa), Greptile, Cursor BugBot, review subagents, custom slash commands.
opportunity: Offer a configurable, vendor-agnostic review service that runs a second model on each change, posts inline comments and escalates only risky PRs.

title: Agent-written tests are weak or silently weakened
problem: Agents write trivial, mocked or flawed tests and weaken tests to pass, so verification is shallow.
current_solutions: Separate test-writing agents, mutation testing, nightly low-signal pruning
opportunity: Build a test-quality auditor with mutation checks and immutable, spec-derived tests.

title: Agents too hard for non-coders to adopt
problem: Agent setup needs config files and connectors, and mainstream users shallowly use AI and don't know what agents can do.
current_solutions: Managed bot platforms, Claude Dispatch, skill files
opportunity: Build one-click onboarding and discovery of agent workflows and simple task-specific apps.

title: Peer review under strain and AI-assisted reviewing
problem: Peer review suffers from volume, poor reviewer matching, low-quality or LLM-written reviews, biased decisions and unclear AI norms. Reviewers also lack tools to check literature coverage or proofs.
who: reviewers, authors, and conference and journal organizers
current_solutions: AI reviewers with human review; reviewer incentives; OpenReview; EMNLP 2026 LLM review experiment; GPT-5.5 Pro paper audits; Google Scholar Labs; Semantic Scholar
opportunity: Build reviewer-matching, review-quality, appeal tracking and AI paper-audit tools with human oversight.

title: Vertical AI needs deep customization and forward deployment
problem: Enterprise and professional customers want custom builds that vendors struggle to deliver at scale, so AI deployment depends on costly embedded engineers.
who: AI vendors and enterprises deploying AI
current_solutions: Forward-deployed engineers; Harvey use-case libraries; no-code configuration on shared primitives; design partners
opportunity: Productize forward deployment with templates and tooling that turn customer-specific work into reusable features, or offer managed deployment services.

title: Verifying compute and pacing agreements
problem: Coordinated slowdowns lack tools to verify compute, hidden training and compliance.
current_solutions: Memory threshold proposals, attestable output proofs
opportunity: Build verification, telemetry and attestation tooling for compute thresholds.

title: MCP server and client debugging friction
problem: MCP has auth bugs, failing inspectors, SDK issues, context-heavy tool descriptions and weak testing and publishing support.
current_solutions: Glama Inspector, mcp-explorer CLI, McpSwitcher, self-fixes with Claude.
opportunity: Build an MCP inspector and testing toolkit with auth recovery, task simulation and context-cost analysis.

title: Leaderboard aggregation and eval registry tooling
problem: Results are scattered across sites without shared schema, provenance, history or pricing.
current_solutions: LMArena Chrome extension, Hugging Face Community Evals, HELM, Inspect AI
opportunity: Build an aggregator with shared schema, historical snapshots, pricing and provenance.

title: Private local-first assistants for sensitive data
problem: Users want to process finance, health, email, documents and meetings without sending data to the cloud, and want secure agents.
current_solutions: OpenJarvis, local-first agents, Gemma and MedGemma, on-device meeting summarizers, Ollama, OpenClaw
opportunity: Build offline-first apps with bundled small models and sandboxed tools for specific private workflows.

title: Vendor benchmark claims lack independent verification
problem: Vendors self-report, cherry-pick baselines, change charts and omit methodology.
current_solutions: Artificial Analysis and same-prompt independent leaderboards
opportunity: Build an independent re-evaluation tracker that checks claimed scores against standardized runs.

title: Billing, refund, credit expiry and support failures at AI vendors
problem: AI vendors have overcharges, cancellations that still bill, expiring prepaid credits, denied refunds, failed payments and slow or bot-only support. Users get locked out or lose money they paid.
who: paying users and teams of AI subscriptions and API credits
current_solutions: Chasing refunds by email, support tickets, multiple accounts, third-party subscriptions that risk suspension
opportunity: Build a subscription and credit management tool that tracks renewals, expiry, cancellations and refunds and helps with disputes, possibly with outcome-verified auto-refunds or rollover wallets.

title: Same model varies in quality across inference providers
problem: The same model differs in speed, quality, quantization and tool-call behavior across hosts and aggregators, and providers rarely publish benchmarks or serving configs. Users can't tell what they are really getting.
who: developers and teams using OpenRouter or third-party hosted open models
current_solutions: Pinning a provider, Kimi vendor verifier, Artificial Analysis benchmarks, falling back to first-party APIs, self-hosting
opportunity: Build a continuous independent benchmarking service that tests provider endpoints for fidelity, speed, tool-call correctness and feature support and publishes results.

title: Voice assistants lack natural turn-taking
problem: Voice agents interrupt, respond awkwardly, miss emotion and sound unnatural, while newer voice models are slow to reach apps.
current_solutions: Cartesia, full-duplex models, GPT-Realtime-2, Gemini Live, Spokenly
opportunity: Build open voice stacks with better turn-taking, wake words and emotion detection.

title: Frontier models fail at spatial, counting and visual detail tasks
problem: Models miscount objects, miss fine visual details, misread layouts and plots, and draw poor diagrams. These failures limit visual and spatial work.
who: developers and scientists applying VLMs to images, plots and layouts
current_solutions: Checking with Python; agentic vision loops that crop and zoom; bounding-box and counting grounding tools
opportunity: Build evals and tool-augmented pipelines that expose and compensate for what VLMs fail to see, count or lay out.

title: Keeping up with AI news without noise or hype
problem: AI news and product launches are overwhelming and hype-toned. People want curated, filterable digests on emerging tech.
current_solutions: news.smol.ai, Gemini scheduled summaries, HN digests, Techpresso, RSS readers, newsletters, web-change monitors
opportunity: Build a personalized, low-noise AI news digest agent with topic filtering that can also exclude AI topics.

title: Prompt and skill optimization lacks eval rigor
problem: Prompts, instruction files and skills are tuned by vibes and degrade silently across models.
current_solutions: DSPy, GEPA, skill test-and-rewrite loops
opportunity: Build a harness that A/B tests prompt and skill changes with metrics.

title: Cheap, accurate PDF and document parsing for agents
problem: Getting reliable text, tables, layout, reading order and charts out of PDFs and Office files is hard. Frontier and VLM parsing is slow, costly and error-prone.
who: developers building agents and RAG pipelines over documents
current_solutions: LiteParse, LlamaParse, Nutrient, Deep Extract, Mistral OCR, PDF.js/Tesseract.js, Gemini extraction with cross-checks, routing simple pages to cheap parsers and complex ones to VLMs
opportunity: Build a cost-aware parsing API that routes pages by complexity and returns grounded layout, coordinates, confidence and cross-checked numbers.

title: RAM and GPU price spikes hurt hardware buyers
problem: AI demand has driven up DRAM, storage and GPU prices, making upgrades and local rigs unaffordable and pushing people to cloud.
who: DIY builders, local-model users, small projects
current_solutions: Buying used or refurbished parts, switching to cloud inference.
opportunity: Build a price tracker and alert service with used-hardware sourcing guides.

title: Absorbing and reviewing the flood of agent output
problem: AI output volume exceeds human capacity to read and review, and agent reports and shared artifacts are hard to render and share.
who: people supervising agents and sharing their outputs
current_solutions: Asking for HTML, diagrams or plain English, Eraser Diagrams, Gist rendering, visual explainer skills, comment-on-HTML review
opportunity: Build a reading and publishing layer that turns agent output into compact, visual, shareable documents and consolidates decisions for approval.

title: Streaming giant MoE models from SSD and offloading experts
problem: Trillion-scale and large MoE models do not fit consumer RAM or VRAM, so people build fragile custom loaders that stream experts from SSD at low throughput. Extreme quants are used alongside, with unpredictable speed and quality.
who: enthusiasts running huge open models on laptops, Macs and small GPUs
current_solutions: DwarfStar SSD streaming, llama.cpp expert offload and GPU cache, Strata expert placement, n-gram tables on NVMe, Unsloth dynamic quants, Apple LLM-in-a-flash, custom C engines
opportunity: Build a packaged runtime with an autotuner that places and caches experts across VRAM, RAM and SSD and predicts speed per machine.

title: Research and analyst agents for reports and monitoring
problem: Analysts and researchers want agents that synthesize filings, data and papers into reports, comparisons and monitoring, and make results easy to check.
current_solutions: Per-deal CLAUDE.md with MCP subagents, Monitor by Parallel, research-agent armies, Codex for papers, Refine, tabular review tools
opportunity: Build vertical research agents with always-on monitoring, row-and-column bulk review and cited structured outputs.

title: Reward hacking and flawed RL environments
problem: RL and RLVR training lets models exploit weak rewards, hardcode test outputs or learn from bugged, unsolvable tasks. Nobody systematically audits environments or rewards, and fixes are patched one hack at a time.
who: labs and teams running RL post-training
current_solutions: LLM judges on tool-call intent, checkpoint rollbacks, inoculation prompting, KL terms and clipping, format rewards, safeagents guard
opportunity: Build tooling that audits RL environments and reward functions for solvability and exploits and monitors rollouts for hacking during training.

title: AI materials discovery and self-driving labs
problem: Materials discovery is slow, simulations like DFT are inaccurate, predicted materials may not be synthesizable, and process details and negative results go unshared. No AlphaFold-style materials model exists.
current_solutions: ML force fields; Periodic Labs; Ginkgo autonomous lab; Lila Sciences; TorchSim; JAX-MD; self-driving labs
opportunity: Build tools for synthesizability and stability checks, automated DFT and closed-loop lab workflows with feedback from failures.

title: Agentic software factories from ticket to release
problem: Teams want agents to handle tickets, PRs, CI and alerts with humans writing specs, but nobody has figured out the full pipeline. Token costs are high.
who: engineering teams and enterprises automating software production
current_solutions: In-house headless harnesses, Flue, Factory.ai, StrongDM Software Factory, OpenAI Symphony, Sentry-triggered agents
opportunity: Build a platform guiding setup of ticket-to-review-to-release agent pipelines with human gates and cost analytics.

title: Ads as a business model for AI chatbots
problem: Free chatbots need funding but ad targeting is unproven, advertisers lack performance data, and users worry ads influence answers.
who: AI chat providers, advertisers and users
current_solutions: Koah native ads, Sourcegraph free tier ads, hybrid subscription plus ads, ad-free positioning
opportunity: Build ad networks and attribution analytics for conversational AI.

title: Agents can't show proof their UI work functions
problem: Agents cannot see or operate the UI they build, so frontend failures go unnoticed and reviewers lack evidence the change works.
who: developers using agents for frontend and app work, and their reviewers
current_solutions: Demo videos and screenshots (Cursor, Showboat, Rodney), Playwright, Chrome MCP, computer use, uiautomator dumps.
opportunity: Build a drop-in toolkit giving agents screenshots, UI state and recordings, attached to PRs as reviewable evidence.

title: Fine-tuning library bugs, version breaks and cryptic errors
problem: Unsloth, TRL, DeepSpeed and similar stacks break on installs, versions, tokenizers, collators, dtypes, vision models and exports, and users waste compute diagnosing them. LoRA parameter counts can also look wrong.
who: people fine-tuning models with open-source libraries
current_solutions: Version pinning, manual patches, Docker setups, Discord troubleshooting, Unsloth fixes
opportunity: Build a pre-flight validator and debugger that catches config, version, tokenizer, template, dataset schema and export problems before compute is spent.

title: Aider stalled; users seek alternatives and gaps
problem: Aider appears abandoned, with missing MCP, OAuth and session features and provider issues.
current_solutions: OpenCode, Claude Code, Aider-CE, wrapping Aider in MCP agents.
opportunity: Maintain a community fork or successor with MCP, OAuth and auto file add.

title: Arena Elo is gameable and does not reflect real usefulness
problem: Vote-based arenas measure chat preference, can be gamed, and miss agentic and long-context quality.
current_solutions: Windsurf Arena Mode, Arena Pareto charts, task-specific bake-offs
opportunity: Build task-grounded, domain or personal arenas with reproducible scoring.

title: Jagged, unpredictable model capabilities
problem: Models excel at hard tasks yet fail easy ones, so users cannot predict where they are reliable and deployment is unpredictable.
opportunity: Build capability-profiling tools that map where a model is reliable for a given workflow.

title: Measuring whether local models match frontier on your tasks
problem: Users report local models matching cloud ones for everyday work, but claims are anecdotal and people lack measurements to decide when local suffices.
who: developers and teams deciding between local and cloud
current_solutions: Intelligence-per-watt studies, personal agents on Qwen 27B, own-domain benchmarking
opportunity: Build a tool where users run their own tasks across local and cloud models and compare quality, cost and speed.

title: GPU compute markets, depreciation and residual value are unclear
problem: GPU compute is illiquid and non-standard, depreciation and capex payback are uncertain, and buyers cannot hedge price or availability.
who: GPU owners, renters, startups and compute financiers
current_solutions: Secured debt for hardware, SF Compute standardized futures, cash-settled derivatives
opportunity: Build a compute marketplace with standardized contracts, price indexes, forwards and GPU asset valuation tools.

title: Media literacy and misleading AI outputs
problem: AI summaries, recaps and hallucinated facts mislead users, and readers can't judge sourcing.
current_solutions: Community Notes, custom prompts, thinking mode
opportunity: Build verification layers that check claims against sources.

title: GPU rental price and compute cost transparency
problem: GPU prices are volatile and opaque, published indices diverge from what users pay, and companies lack tools to track compute cost and margins.
who: AI startups, GPU buyers and inference providers
current_solutions: Ornn and Silicon Data price indexes, serverless GPU inference, self-hosting
opportunity: Build a GPU price index and TCO tracker using prices paid, utilization and demand data.

title: Long-context local inference limited by KV cache
problem: KV cache memory and prefill cost limit long context on consumer hardware, quantizing it may hurt quality, and prompt caches fail.
who: local users running long agent sessions
current_solutions: Q8/Q4 KV cache, TurboQuant, dynamic KV management, cache-stable prompts, prompt-cache patches
opportunity: Build tooling that profiles KV cost, tests quant impact on the user's workload and applies the best compression and cache strategy.

title: AI research agents lack taste, persistence and original ideas
problem: Agents do engineering and experiments well but pick poor problems, commit early, ignore feedback and budgets, and struggle to generate important ideas.
current_solutions: Human-assigned directions; prompt corrections; multi-agent exploration; design-doc-first workflow
opportunity: Build harnesses with budget tracking, persistence and idea ranking to help agents or humans select research directions.

title: Chatbot personality, tone and style controls
problem: Users dislike default personalities, repeated stylistic tics and fixed presets, and custom instructions often fail. Some are attached to a specific model's tone that cannot be ported.
current_solutions: Custom instructions, attempts to transfer 4o personas into Claude
opportunity: Build a front end or rewriter with personality sliders and a style layer that reproduces a preferred voice across assistants.

title: Gemini app quality and integration gaps
problem: Gemini's consumer app has weak default thinking, limits, file caps, poor Google integrations and instruction-ignoring behavior.
current_solutions: Google AI Studio, Gemini Personal Intelligence beta, switching to ChatGPT or Claude
opportunity: Build a front end exposing higher thinking, large files and persistent projects on Gemini models.

title: AI incident tracking, reporting and whistleblower channels
problem: Incident disclosures are incomplete, with no shared standard and no safe channel for employees to report risks.
current_solutions: Voluntary reports
opportunity: Build an independent public incident tracker and secure reporting and routing platform.

title: Bureaucratic and personal paperwork automation
problem: Forms, permits, reimbursements and routine admin take heavy time and give unclear answers.
who: parents, small businesses and individuals dealing with administration
current_solutions: Manus autofill, agent-drafted correction emails, Codex and Claude Code with browser control, virtual cards
opportunity: Build domain-specific agents that navigate permits and forms and handle reimbursements with review.

title: Teams lack shared memory and tacit knowledge for agents
problem: Institutional knowledge, SOPs and decisions live in people's heads or get lost when answers are shared or employees leave. Every agent chat needs re-explaining.
who: teams and companies deploying agents, and product teams handing context to agents
current_solutions: WorkIQ, Granola MCP, Notion as an operating system, Zapier Shared Brain, ContextMCP, AI assistants answering new-hire questions
opportunity: Build a shared company-memory layer capturing SOPs, decisions and product context with permissions preserved for agents.

title: Cheap near-frontier and open model tiers as cost cutters
problem: Teams want near-frontier quality at a fraction of the price using cheap tier models, fine-tuning or hosted open models, but need to know which fits each workload.
current_solutions: Gemini Flash, Haiku, DeepSeek V4 Flash, GLM, Together and Fireworks fine-tuning, Tinker, hosted open-model providers
opportunity: Build a migration tool that benchmarks a workload on cheaper models and automates distillation or hosting.

title: Customizable always-on personal and coworker agents
problem: Users want persistent, customizable agents with memory and accounts, but they either do little or act intrusively.
current_solutions: Hermes Agent, OpenAI dots, Grok Bot, per-agent cloud machines
opportunity: Build an open assistant with persistent memory, scheduling and controllable proactivity.

title: Local AI setup too hard for non-technical users
problem: Most people cannot install and configure local models, and want one-click suites covering chat, documents, agents, search and home inference.
current_solutions: Ollama, LM Studio, Unsloth Desktop, TextGen, LlamaBarn, llama.app, Nativ
opportunity: Ship a one-click local AI app or home box with auto-configuration and bundled capabilities.

title: Agent safety standards, liability and AI insurance
problem: Insurers and enterprises lack an accepted standard for AI risk, and liability for AI harms is unclear.
current_solutions: AIUC-1 standard, mutual insurance proposals
opportunity: Build certification, testing, underwriting and recourse products around agent safety standards.

title: Enterprise and vertical agent platforms
problem: Enterprise back-office and domain agents are built bespoke, with shared context, release process and governance missing.
who: enterprises and domain teams in legal, finance and operations
current_solutions: Slack intake bots, ChatGPT Workspace Agents, bespoke builds
opportunity: Offer standardized vertical agent templates with evals, versioned releases, identity and audit.

title: Dependency and package supply-chain attacks
problem: Malicious packages hit developers within hours of publication, and unpinned dependencies and actions make updates risky. Verifying maintainers and patched builds is hard.
current_solutions: Dependabot/Renovate delays, pip --uploaded-prior-to, Socket, version pinning, lockfile audits, npm scanners.
opportunity: Build a tool that enforces cooldowns, pins actions, flags suspicious new releases and maintainer changes, and tracks patched versions.

title: Opaque, uncontrollable and non-portable AI memory
problem: Cross-chat memory mixes unrelated information, goes stale, leaks across projects and cannot be viewed, edited, scoped or migrated between assistants.
who: chatbot users and people switching assistants
current_solutions: ChatGPT Projects, custom instructions, disabling history, Anthropic memory import, export prompts
opportunity: Build an editable, portable memory manager to view, scope, toggle and migrate what assistants remember.

title: Data retention rules block regulated and zero-retention enterprises
problem: Mandatory 30-day retention, subprocessors and vendor reuse of data conflict with enterprise zero-data-retention policies. Sensitive or regulated data cannot be sent to frontier APIs, and zero-retention terms cost extra.
who: enterprises in regulated sectors and security or compliance teams
current_solutions: Paying premiums for zero retention; contract negotiation over trajectory data; enterprises taking on retention themselves; private hosting on Azure
opportunity: Build a gateway or proxy that routes sensitive workloads to zero-retention models and gives auditable evidence of data flows.

title: Eval results are noisy and non-deterministic
problem: Repeated runs give different results, timings vary, and scores lack uncertainty, so one-off numbers and regression tests are unreliable.
current_solutions: Low temperature, fixed seeds, repeated runs, confidence intervals
opportunity: Provide a CI eval runner that repeats trials and reports confidence, variance and stable timing.

title: Media recommendations beyond single scores
problem: Review scores poorly predict personal taste, spoilers and discovery are poor.
current_solutions: Letterboxd cross-checking, Claude skills, Claude for fiction
opportunity: Build a taste-aware, spoiler-safe recommender with multi-dimensional ratings and collection cataloging.

title: Local inference is slow at prefill and long context
problem: Prompt processing, model loading and long-context decode are slow on Macs, CPUs, Strix Halo and consumer GPUs, and decode-only benchmarks hide it. Mac clustering tools are unmaintained.
who: local LLM users on Apple Silicon and consumer hardware
current_solutions: ANE-assisted prefill, Metal backends, MLX, RDMA over Thunderbolt, batch size tuning, LMCache
opportunity: Build a local runtime and profiler tuned for fast prefill, model switching and Mac clustering that reports TTFT as well as decode speed.

title: Measuring quality loss from quantization and compression
problem: Perplexity hides failures in quantized or modified local models, and speed claims are inconsistent.
current_solutions: KL divergence, llama.cpp perplexity, OpenCompass, personal quant benchmarks
opportunity: Build a reproducible quant-quality suite reporting KLD, task accuracy and long-context impact.

title: Continual learning from deployment and catastrophic forgetting
problem: Deployed models do not learn from production traces or corrections, and online fine-tuning causes forgetting. Teams are unsure whether to put knowledge in weights or context.
who: teams running production models and agents
current_solutions: Cursor's online RL, Baseten trace self-improvement, clinician-edit flywheels, replay data, OpenClaw-RL
opportunity: Build a feedback-to-weights pipeline that captures traces, trains periodic updates with replay and measures forgetting.

title: Scalable verifiable RL environments: creation and infrastructure
problem: RL scaling needs thousands of realistic, verifiable environments that are slow to build by hand and mostly exist for code and math. Environment infrastructure is also buggy and hard to debug.
current_solutions: Hugging Face Hub environments, Prime Intellect env hub, Atropos, synthetic environment generators, bought environments, Modal sandboxes
opportunity: Build a platform that generates, versions, shares and load-tests verifiable RL environments from repos, text or domain data.

title: Permission prompt fatigue and unclear approval controls
problem: Approving every action is tedious, but skipping permissions is risky and auto modes are opaque.
current_solutions: Claude Code auto mode, Codex guardian, allow/deny lists, YOLO flags.
opportunity: Build a policy tool that pre-approves safe patterns, explains blocks and escalates risky actions.

title: Mojo language and tooling gaps
problem: Mojo lacks Windows support, compiler bindings, core features and mature docs, with bugs and weak Python interop.
current_solutions: Python module workarounds, custom cpython bindings, reading stdlib code.
opportunity: A community Windows port, libmojo-style library, or Mojo guides and interop tooling.

title: Routing routine work to local models, hard work to frontier
problem: Teams want to cut spend by sending easy tasks to local or cheap models and hard ones to frontier, but routing is ad hoc.
who: developers and teams with mixed local and cloud usage
current_solutions: Manual switching, semantic routers, BERT classifier routers, cloud burst, small router models
opportunity: Build a router that classifies tasks and dispatches to local or cloud models with cost and quality tracking.

title: Robots lack reliability, generalization and real-world data
problem: Robots generalize poorly, lack touch and other sensing, need many demonstrations, and academic robotics lacks real-world validation and good simulators.
current_solutions: Hierarchical RL policies; diffusion transformer action generation; VLAs; video-plus-action models
opportunity: Build one-shot demonstration learning, reliability testing and shared real-world benchmarks for robots.

title: Personal finance, bills and subscription management
problem: Bills, subscriptions and bank interfaces are fragmented, and users want assistants that analyze, warn and cancel without sharing passwords.
current_solutions: ChatGPT finance preview, Attain Finance
opportunity: Build a finance agent that aggregates accounts, tracks bills and cancels hidden subscriptions securely.

title: Game and simulated-business environments for agent benchmarks
problem: Game and simulation benchmarks lack fidelity, fair budgets and replay methodology.
current_solutions: Baldur's Gate 3 harness, Vending-Bench, FoodTruck Bench, MineBench, WoW MCP
opportunity: Build a standard game and simulation harness with budget modes, replays and scoring.

title: llama.cpp lag, breakage and GGUF compatibility
problem: New models lack day-zero llama.cpp support, need forks or specific PRs, and GGUFs ship broken or need re-downloads after template fixes.
who: users running new open models locally
current_solutions: Reading commits, forks, waiting, Unsloth fixes, community ports
opportunity: Build a compatibility tracker and validator mapping versions to supported models, GGUFs, templates and breaking changes.
