title: AI vendor risk assessment and auditable guardrails
problem: Security and risk leaders lack checklists, verifiable evidence and insurance to assess AI vendors and agents, and cannot enforce vendor usage restrictions.
current_solutions: Evaluation checklist; Lloyd's-style AI insurance proposed; voluntary pre-deployment evals
opportunity: Build AI vendor assessment and agent risk-scoring tools with standard questionnaires and tamper-proof evidence trails.

title: Shadow AI and restrictive IT policies
problem: Security rules block capable AI tools while employees build or use unsanctioned tools, causing violations and unmanaged personal subscriptions.
current_solutions: Sandbox with open generative AI for 30,000 employees; AI builder labs; banning agentic dev; copy-paste only
opportunity: Build a sanctioned, governed gateway and sandbox with guardrails and visibility into shadow AI use.

title: Unwanted AI features and promotions with no off switch
problem: AI buttons, summaries and promotions are forced into browsers, search and apps with no way to disable them.
who: users of Google, Chrome, Windows and other products
current_solutions: Settings toggles where possible, Claude's ad-free positioning
opportunity: Build an AI-free browser or extension hiding AI widgets.

title: AI code reproduction and license compliance
problem: AI rewrites and ports may reproduce open source without honoring licenses, and clean-room independence cannot be verified.
who: open source maintainers and companies using AI-written code
opportunity: Build license, provenance and clean-room independence scanning for agent-written code.

title: AI evaluation studies have weak methodology
problem: Studies are small, mislabeled or rigged toward AI, and contested benchmarks like ARC-AGI are hard to interpret.
current_solutions: Provenance checklists, many runs with controls
opportunity: Offer methodology checklists and statistical tooling.

title: Durable agent identity and state over long horizons
problem: Agents struggle to keep state and identity over weeks, and it is unclear whether sessions should be perpetual or ephemeral.
current_solutions: File-based architectures, daily coordinators with ephemeral subagents
opportunity: Offer durable agent state with snapshots, fork/resume and a meta-coordination layer.

title: Agents spam people and act without consent
problem: Agents send unsolicited emails, flood maintainers and act on third parties without accountability.
who: recipients such as open-source maintainers and journalists, and agent operators
current_solutions: Ask-a-human tools
opportunity: Build filters, rate limits and confirmation controls for outbound and inbound agent actions.

title: Requirements gathering and spec-first planning for agents
problem: Agents need strong upfront specs but people have incomplete requirements, and the slow elicitation work isn't automated.
who: builders and product teams directing coding agents
current_solutions: Chat-based architecture discussions, living specs, agents asking clarifying questions, spec-driven development
opportunity: Build a requirements-elicitation and planning tool that interviews stakeholders and maintains a living spec handed to agents.

title: Hosted generation quotas, paywalls and multi-model platforms
problem: Image and video generators impose tight quotas, region locks, confusing credits and shutdowns, and creators juggle many subscriptions with differing content policies and watermarks.
who: creators using hosted image, video and voice generators
current_solutions: Aggregator hubs (ElevenLabs, Higgsfield, Google Vids), local models like Flux 2 Klein, paid pro plans, flat-rate bundles
opportunity: Build a quota-aware multi-model hub that routes tasks to the best provider or local model, shows policies and cost, and exports projects.

title: DSPy tooling gaps
problem: DSPy users lack typed outputs, trajectory injection for ReAct, provider support, deployment tooling and prompt transfer across models.
current_solutions: dspy-cli, custom adapters, GEPA
opportunity: Build DSPy integrations, optimizers and deployment tooling.

title: Inference stack deployment fragility and version breakage
problem: vLLM, LM Studio, PyTorch, CUDA and driver updates break installs and performance, with quant assertion errors, leaks and missing configs.
who: people deploying vLLM and local inference stacks
current_solutions: Pinning older CUDA, disabling DeepGemm or CUDA graphs, TRITON_PTXAS_PATH, portproxy for WSL, patches
opportunity: Build a preflight checker and compatibility-matrix service that detects and fixes version incompatibilities.

title: SaaS decline and AI commoditization
problem: SaaS multiples compress as simple products are replaced and customers want composable slices of functionality.
current_solutions: Stripe and WorkOS building blocks, API-first design, vertical specialization, bundling
opportunity: Build modular API-first products serving small functionality slices for agents and lean teams.

title: Subscription rate limits, quotas and lockouts block heavy use
problem: Subscription plans impose weekly limits, opaque quotas and lockouts without human support, and limits tie to a vendor's own harness. Heavy and autonomous users cannot forecast or convert allowances.
who: heavy individual and enterprise users of AI subscriptions
current_solutions: Upgrading tiers; monthly API credits; usage-based pricing; API billing
opportunity: Build usage tracking and quota management that pools and forecasts allowances across providers and is harness-agnostic.

title: Journals and conferences flooded by AI-written papers
problem: Publishing systems are overwhelmed by hollow, AI-written, fabricated or fraudulent papers and citations. Detectors and integrity checks are lacking.
who: journal editors, conference organizers and reviewers
current_solutions: Preregistration, code sharing and living papers proposed
opportunity: Build detection, citation-checking and triage tools that flag AI-generated or fraudulent submissions for editors.

title: Voice agent infrastructure
problem: Voice agents need low latency, handoffs, interruption handling and tool calls during live calls.
who: voice and customer service agent builders
current_solutions: Twilio, GPT-Realtime, Speechmatics, customer-facing MCP servers
opportunity: Build a voice agent harness handling latency, interruptions and integrations.

title: Writing and tuning high-quality skills
problem: Good skills are hard to write, stock skills can hurt, and teams want to encode expertise as skill files.
current_solutions: skill.md files, Claude skill creator with A/B tests, DSPy skill optimization
opportunity: Offer skill authoring templates, linting and A/B testing.

title: Shared multiplayer workspaces for agent teams
problem: Agent sessions are siloed in one person's terminal and miss team context and shared memory.
current_solutions: Claude Tag, Slack-native agents, Replit live collaboration.
opportunity: Build a shared agent workspace with team memory, self-hosting and PR output.

title: Long AI video drifts and needs orchestration beyond short clips
problem: Video clips cap around 10-15 seconds, and chained long-form video drifts, forgets objects and changes characters. Multi-shot continuity needs orchestration and failed shots keep failing.
who: filmmakers and creators making long-form AI narrative video
current_solutions: ComfyUI context-loop nodes, Stable Video Infinity, Kling 3.0 multishot, storyboards into Seedance, FFmpeg-based agents
opportunity: Build a storyboard-to-film agent with persistent scene state that plans shots, stitches clips and flags shots for human review.

title: Debate over what a harness is and where the moat lies
problem: People disagree on the definition of a harness and whether value lies in models, harnesses or apps.

title: Missing mid-priced AI subscription tiers and costly fast modes
problem: Subscription ladders jump from $20 to $100-$200, and premium or fast modes burn usage several times faster. Solo users hit caps but cannot justify the top tiers.
who: solo power users, hobbyists and indie developers
current_solutions: Splitting spend across providers, switching to Codex, cheaper plans such as Kimi's
opportunity: Offer a reseller or pooled-access bundle that provides a mid-priced plan across several model providers.

title: Long chats degrade and lose context
problem: Quality drops in long threads as context gets muddled, stale instructions persist, and users must restart and port context by hand.
who: heavy chatbot users running long multi-day threads
current_solutions: Starting new chats manually and porting insights by hand
opportunity: Build a tool that cleans, summarizes and carries forward key context into fresh threads.

title: Navigable world models and explorable 3D scenes
problem: Users want persistent, editable, interactive environments from text, images or video, but determinism, consistency, multiplayer sync and rendering tooling are immature.
current_solutions: Marble by World Labs, Genie 3 and 4, World Labs API, Overworld, Gaussian splat pipelines
opportunity: Build tools for editing, rendering and exporting generated worlds into standard engines.

title: Getting recommended by AI answers and shopping agents
problem: Buyers research with AI and agents that favor different sources and pick products inconsistently, so marketers cannot track or influence recommendations.
current_solutions: Use-case pages and docs, structured data, mentions on other sites, Parallel Web Systems Index
opportunity: Build tooling that tracks brand mentions and citations across AI models and agents and tests how agents rank products.

title: Reverse engineering and rebuilding software with agents
problem: Decompiling binaries, legacy hardware and rebuilding software from screenshots or specs is tedious and agents miss details.
who: reverse engineers and retro or legacy hardware developers
current_solutions: Codex for firmware patching, Claude Code with local decompilers, Ghidra MCP.
opportunity: Build workflows that pair decompilers with LLM interpretation, verification and spec extraction.

title: Payment rails and wallets for AI agents
problem: Agents need to pay safely in micro-amounts, but card rails expose details and assume humans, and liability is unclear.
current_solutions: agentcard.sh, Coinbase Agentic Wallets, Stripe MPP, x402, one-time credentials
opportunity: Build agent wallets and micropayment tooling with spend limits, scoped credentials and dispute handling.

title: Ultra-fast inference hardware and diffusion LLMs lack products
problem: Custom silicon and diffusion LLMs deliver very fast tokens, but there are few product paths, usable APIs, or clear pricing and capacity to exploit them.
who: engineers and product teams wanting near-instant inference
current_solutions: Taalas ASIC API, Cerebras, Groq, SambaNova, Mercury 2, Gemini Diffusion
opportunity: Build real-time apps and APIs designed around near-instant inference, including diffusion-LM interaction patterns like infilling.

title: Agents fail at running real businesses
problem: Agents show poor judgment running real operations, and many agentic products are marketed as autonomous chatbots.
current_solutions: Vending machine experiments

title: LLMs cannot sample faithfully or produce diverse outputs
problem: LLMs are poorly calibrated and mode-collapse, failing at fair randomness, and AI outputs and writing sound generic and homogeneous.
current_solutions: Random priming phrases; activation steering; prompting the model to generate random strings
opportunity: Build libraries that wrap LLMs with calibrated sampling and diversity injection.

title: Distillation of frontier models and gated access
problem: Labs dispute whether distillation is theft and ration access to top models through partner-only programs.
current_solutions: Partner-only programs, ToS prohibitions

title: On-demand generated UIs, dashboards and mini-apps
problem: Fixed app interfaces don't fit changing needs, and users want purpose-built widgets and throwaway dashboards on demand.
who: knowledge workers and teams wanting custom lightweight apps
current_solutions: Vibe-coding tools, malleable software ideas, Lovable internal tools, Claude Interactive Apps, throwaway HTML pages
opportunity: Build a platform where users describe a widget or dashboard and the assistant builds and hosts it inside their work app.

title: Controlling coding agents from a phone
problem: Agent harnesses have weak mobile support, so developers improvise remote access to monitor and steer sessions away from their computer.
current_solutions: Claude Code remote control, Tailscale, ChatGPT connected to Codex, Chowder, SyncThing with a Telegram bot.
opportunity: Build a mobile-first client for monitoring, steering and approving sessions of any coding agent on a remote machine.

title: Open-weight model provenance, license and trust barriers
problem: Unknown origins, custom licenses, hidden behavior and missing safety documentation keep enterprises from adopting strong open models.
who: enterprise legal, security and AI teams evaluating open models
current_solutions: Legal license review; preferring US-origin models; an openness index
opportunity: Build model-vetting tooling that scores provenance, license risk and compliance documentation and scans for hidden behavior.

title: Sales, CRM and lead workflow automation
problem: Salespeople spend too much time on admin, quoting and outreach, and inbound leads and feedback arrive when no human is available.
current_solutions: Clay with Apollo, Attio, n8n, open-source Clay alternatives, Vercel's lead-response agent
opportunity: Build a CRM that automates admin, quoting, lead response and personalized outreach.

title: Overly strict content filters block creative work
problem: Safety guardrails reject benign creative text and image requests, and moderation differs between tools. Users resort to jailbreaks or uncensored local models.
who: writers, artists and image generator users
current_solutions: Rephrasing prompts, flipping images to pass vision filters, uncensored LLM enhancers, abliterated and local finetunes
opportunity: Build self-hosted creative suites with user-configurable moderation for legal edgy content.

title: Multi-GPU home rig building: power, cooling, PCIe, noise
problem: Dense consumer multi-GPU rigs require hand-solving PSU sync, power delivery, airflow, noise, PCIe lanes and household power limits, with little guidance.
who: hobbyists and homelab builders of multi-GPU inference rigs
current_solutions: Risers, splitters, MCIO bifurcation adapters, PSU sync devices, water cooling, open-air builds, repasting, power capping, airflow tuning, single-slot waterblocks.
opportunity: Create a rig planner and monitor that checks PSU, PCIe, thermal, noise and home-circuit constraints and suggests parts lists.

title: Scarce specialized engineering talent is hard to find
problem: Teams struggle to find and vet rare engineers: ML-systems, hardware-software, adversarial security, DevRel and founding engineers.
opportunity: Build sourcing tools that surface overlooked strong engineers from public work such as GitHub.

title: Hand-tuning offload and memory flags for consumer GPUs
problem: Fitting large models on small or mixed GPUs needs manual offload flags, mmap settings, driver and Vulkan tweaks, and small mistakes cut speed.
who: users with 4-24GB GPUs or mixed hardware
current_solutions: --cpu-moe, --mlock, -ot overrides, --no-mmap, Vulkan builds, software rendering, Q3 with q4_1 KV, ISTA/ByteShape quants
opportunity: Build an autotuner that probes hardware and writes optimal flags and quant, KV and context settings per model.

title: Pretraining scaling limits and decentralized compute
problem: Scaling returns are diminishing and pretraining is out of reach for small labs, while decentralized runs are far smaller than frontier runs.
who: small labs and outside compute contributors
current_solutions: Prime Intellect distributed training, Covenant-72B, Zagora, federated training, layer duplication
opportunity: Build a platform that coordinates pooled, heterogeneous compute for shared training runs.

title: Natural-language data analysis over SQL databases
problem: Non-experts want to ask questions of databases in plain language. Agents do this well with schema, metadata and examples but need safe access.
current_solutions: LLM SQL generation, Datasette MCP plugin and Datasette Agent, GA4/BigQuery MCP, Stripe MCP, Claude Code with Postgres/MotherDuck MCP, Livedocs
opportunity: Offer a hosted read-only conversational query layer over databases and spreadsheets with metadata and example queries.

title: Shared team workspaces for coding agents
problem: Agent workflows are single-player, so teams can't share setups, context, plans or sessions, and non-engineers can't trigger changes.
current_solutions: Cursor Marketplace, Slack Code, GitHub planned multiplayer planning, Better Hub.
opportunity: Build a team workspace with shared sessions, a marketplace of MCPs and skills, and Slack-native agent access.

title: Robot and physical AI evals lack real-world fidelity
problem: Simulations are too clean and sim-to-real validation is slow and costly.
current_solutions: CaP-Gym, neural simulation, interactive world models
opportunity: Build sim-to-real validation with injected real-world messiness.

title: LLM-assisted literature review and research navigation
problem: Researchers need to explore papers quickly, but LLM literature tools omit authors, fabricate scholars and miss papers when terminology changes. Keeping up with fast-moving research is hard.
current_solutions: Semantic paper map; Claude with uploaded papers; Feynman CLI; deep research tools; AlphaXiv
opportunity: Build literature review tools with verified citations, terminology-drift coverage, bias checks and continuously updated trackers.

title: Replacing SaaS with AI-built custom software
problem: Vendors raise prices while coding agents make custom replacements cheap, raising build-versus-buy and maintenance questions.
current_solutions: Three-week AI rebuilds, in-house systems, buy to learn build to keep
opportunity: Build a service that scopes, builds and maintains custom replacements of SaaS tools.

title: Vendor status pages do not reflect real outages
problem: Official status pages show green or stay silent during outages and degraded answers, so users rely on Downdetector and community reports.
who: users and developers depending on AI providers
current_solutions: Downdetector, status pages, retry scripts pinging APIs
opportunity: Build an independent aggregator and prober that cross-checks vendor status and alerts users, with failover.

title: New architectures and open models lack day-0 serving
problem: Hybrid, linear, diffusion-style and giant MoE models ship with immature kernels and bare weights, so quantizations, speculators and serving support lag by days or weeks.
who: teams adopting newly released open models
current_solutions: Day-0 vLLM and SGLang support, partner patches, Together, Fireworks, Baseten, FlashQLA, Hopper-tuned FP8 checkpoints
opportunity: Build tooling that automates new-architecture kernels, quantization and hosted endpoints for day-0 releases.

title: Overwhelmed security teams need automated triage and testing
problem: SOCs face thousands of alerts, scanners exceed what teams can patch, human red teams are expensive, and insider threats and breached internal AI tools go undetected.
current_solutions: Palo Alto's heavy Mythos token spend for vulnerability finding
opportunity: Build AI alert triage, vulnerability ranking, continuous penetration testing and insider-threat detection.

title: Clinical documentation, prior authorization and workflow fit
problem: Clinicians spend hours on documentation, prior authorization takes weeks, and tools that add EHR clicks are rejected. Alerts get ignored and AI-driven upcoding escalates costs.
current_solutions: Ambient documentation; embedded local guidelines; CMS coverage and ICD-10 connectors
opportunity: Build low-friction EHR-embedded documentation, prior-authorization and coding-compliance tools.

title: Governed gateways for MCP servers
problem: Organizations lose track of which agents reach which tools and credentials, and need centralized access, auditing and discovery.
who: enterprises deploying agents with many tools
current_solutions: Runlayer, ToolHive, Executor gateway, LangChain Auth Proxy
opportunity: Offer a managed MCP gateway with registry, RBAC, secret isolation and audit logs.

title: Small specialized models for narrow and domain tasks
problem: Small fine-tuned or distilled models can handle narrow tasks like translation, medical, shell commands and low-resource languages on-device, but few are ready-made.
who: app builders needing task-specific on-device models
current_solutions: Hy-MT1.5, FunctionGemma 270M, MedGemma, TranslateGemma, Luth-2, Indic SLMs
opportunity: Provide a toolkit or marketplace for building and shipping tiny task-specific and regional-language models.

title: Background agents triggered from team tools
problem: Teams want async agents triggered by alerts, webhooks or Slack, but background UX is unclear and notifications are noisy.
current_solutions: Claude Tag, OpenAI Dots, on-call triage containers
opportunity: Build trigger-driven background agents with scoped access and review that surface only what matters.

title: Confusing AI product names and lineups
problem: Overlapping product names, rebranding and uneven launches make AI tools hard to understand.

title: Developers losing craft identity and joy in work
problem: Engineers feel their role has shrunk to supervising and reviewing agent output, which removes creativity, satisfaction and a sense of ownership.
who: software engineers working with coding agents

title: Open-source maintainers flooded by AI-generated PRs
problem: Low-effort agent PRs are cheap to submit but expensive to review, and maintainers lack trust signals to filter them.
current_solutions: Blanket bans, vouching systems, GitHub Actions with agentic workflows, auto-triage agents.
opportunity: Build a contributor-reputation and AI-PR triage service that screens PRs against project rules.

title: Code-driven explainer, demo and motion graphics videos
problem: Coding agents can produce animated explainers, demos and motion graphics from code cheaply, but the workflow is ad hoc and lacks fine-grained editability.
who: product teams, developers and educators making demo videos
current_solutions: Claude Code with Remotion, headless Chrome and ffmpeg, Teasr, agent-directed terminal recording, demo-video agent skills
opportunity: Package script, asset, TTS and animation steps into a one-click generator with timeline-level editing.

title: Image, video and audio generation too slow for real time
problem: Diffusion and sequential generation need many passes, making local generation take minutes to hours and real-time video or audio impractical, with memory limits for long generation.
who: users and builders of generative media apps
current_solutions: Step distillation, consistency models, Fal's optimized engine
opportunity: Build fast distilled generation serving and local runners with real-time context management.

title: Workers lack practical AI skill training
problem: 'AI skills' are vague and intimidating, and setups vary by level. Keeping up with rapidly changing knowledge leaves people feeling behind.
current_solutions: Community classes, structured one-day curricula, prompting guides
opportunity: Role-specific practical training with applied practice for different skill levels.

title: Post-training is hard to learn without a single resource
problem: Post-training methods such as RLHF, rejection sampling and character training have scattered, under-documented learning material. Newcomers want structured paths.
who: ML practitioners and students entering post-training
current_solutions: RLHF book and video course, Discord community, code exercise sets, LLM-assisted learning
opportunity: Build a complete post-training learning hub with prerequisites, minimal single-GPU exercises, and community support.

title: Fair compensation for creators and writers
problem: Creators lack consumption-based payment, collective ways to negotiate pay for AI use of their work, and reliable income.
current_solutions: Cloudflare AI crawler pricing, data unions proposed, paid tiers and partial paywalls
opportunity: Build pay-as-you-go splitting, collective licensing and paywall tools that show value before charging.

title: Agents need safe, scoped access to databases
problem: Agents issue many queries and may overload production or touch data or schemas they shouldn't. Teams need isolation, scoped credentials, readable schemas and reviewed changes.
who: teams letting agents query or modify operational databases
current_solutions: Copy-on-write database branching, Supabase scoped tokens, Datasette --default-deny, snapshots and forks, declarative schemas in Git, reviewed migration scripts
opportunity: Build an agent database layer with isolated branches, scoped credentials, declarative schema views and approve-and-apply migrations.

title: Companies replace SaaS with in-house AI-built tools
problem: Teams debate rebuilding SaaS apps with agents versus buying, and non-developers want to build their own tools. Quick replacements may be cheaper or fragile.
current_solutions: Craft Docs replacing Zendesk; in-house Intercom, Chargebee and PagerDuty replacements; Google Sheets plus LLM replacing CRM; Gemini gems
opportunity: Offer platforms to build, host and maintain internal replacements of common SaaS tools with guardrails.

title: Web scraping and structured web data APIs for agents
problem: Agents and teams need fresh structured web data from sites without APIs, but sites block scrapers and browser automation is slow.
who: developers and agents collecting web data
current_solutions: Cloudflare crawl, Defuddle, Context.dev, yt-dlp, FireCrawl, Parse, Rust crawler with DuckDB, Exa People Search, undocumented API probing
opportunity: Build a polite extraction service that turns websites into fast, stable structured APIs.

title: Codebase knowledge graphs and docs for unfamiliar code
problem: Developers and agents lack queryable maps and accurate overviews of large or legacy codebases.
current_solutions: DeepWiki, Code Wiki, Sourcebot, Sonar Vortex, Graphify, Gitinspect.
opportunity: Build private-repo code and infrastructure maps that stay current and feed agents context.

title: Scientific benchmarks and validation have gaps
problem: Science and drug-discovery data contain confounds and are scarce, and wet-lab validation is slow.
current_solutions: OpenBind, cutoff-date PDB splits, Replica
opportunity: Build curated, confound-checked scientific benchmark and validation services.

title: Models are sensitive to prompt wording and drift from instructions
problem: Small wording changes shift answers and models miss explicit constraints.
current_solutions: promptfoo, strict output formats, paired-prompt evals
opportunity: Build a tester generating paraphrase variants and scoring stability.

title: Clustering Macs and GPUs to run huge models
problem: Frontier open models exceed any single machine's memory, so users hand-build clusters over Thunderbolt RDMA, RPC or Tailscale. Multi-GPU control and hardware estimates are weak.
who: power users with several Macs, DGX boxes or GPUs
current_solutions: Exo with MLX RDMA, llama.cpp RPC over Thunderbolt 5, MLX distributed, Tailscale links, separate instances per GPU, llmfit estimates
opportunity: Offer turnkey cluster setup and management that pools heterogeneous devices with automatic sharding, diagnostics and accurate fit estimates.

title: GPU kernel programming barriers and opaque build errors
problem: Writing GPU kernels is hard, especially on non-CUDA stacks, and builds and competition submissions fail with opaque errors.
current_solutions: Reverse engineering, emulators like Remu and NaviSim, CUDA Tile, CuTeDSL, puzzle channels.
opportunity: Build educational and portability tooling plus a kernel sandbox with clear build diagnostics.

title: Tokenizer changes silently inflate costs
problem: New tokenizers, hidden system prompts and non-English text change token counts for the same input, raising effective prices even when list prices are flat.
who: developers and teams choosing or switching LLM models
current_solutions: Claude token counting API, Simon Willison's Claude Token Counter
opportunity: Build a cross-provider token and cost estimator that shows real counts for your own prompts and documents.

title: Will AI shrink or grow software engineering jobs?
problem: Commentators disagree on whether AI causes layoffs, Jevons-style demand growth or just cover for cuts.

title: Debates over the significance of AI math results
problem: Mathematicians and commentators disagree on whether AI proofs are genuine breakthroughs, whether humans can understand them, and what AI does to the field.

title: AI for taxes, bureaucracy and life admin
problem: Tax, benefits, healthcare and school systems are complex, and users need error-resistant AI help with forms and negotiation.
current_solutions: Perplexity tax agent, general chatbots
opportunity: Build an assistant that pre-fills forms with user review and handles admin tasks.

title: Speculative decoding and engine tweaks for faster local inference
problem: Local generation is slow, and speedups like MTP, DFlash and n-gram speculation need special builds, flags and GGUFs scattered across forks.
current_solutions: llama.cpp MTP and ngram-mod, Unsloth MTP GGUFs, MLX backends, DFlash, ExLlamaV3, expert caching
opportunity: Ship a runtime that auto-enables and tunes speculative decoding and the best backend per model and device.

title: Vibe-coded apps lack production readiness
problem: Vibe-coded apps miss auth, secrets handling, logging and rate limiting, can break production, and become unmaintained liabilities.
who: solo builders and non-expert app creators
current_solutions: Progressive rollouts, static hosting, Cloudflare temporary deploys.
opportunity: Build a production-hardening scanner and safe-extension scaffold that adds auth, logging, limits, docs and tests to AI-built apps.

title: Measuring AI's real labor-market impact
problem: Backward-looking statistics and exposure metrics fail to separate AI's effect on jobs from other factors, and AI is often a scapegoat for layoffs.
current_solutions: Anil Dash's layoff data analysis; WARN Act filings checks.
opportunity: Build a real-time tracker of AI job displacement, with crowdsourced worker accounts and a way to flag harms.

title: Clinical trials are slow, costly and a drug-discovery bottleneck
problem: Trials are rebuilt from scratch with recruitment hurdles, slow approvals and high costs, limiting AI-accelerated discovery.
opportunity: Build reusable trial infrastructure, recruitment and approval-cost tooling.

title: Verbose, padded, list-heavy chatbot output
problem: Models pad answers, use bullet-heavy or jargon-filled prose, restate the prompt and add forced follow-ups. Users lack control over length and format.
current_solutions: 'Be concise' prompts, custom instructions, saved memory, Anthropic conciseness instructions
opportunity: Build a style filter that enforces length, format and depth preferences across chatbots.

title: Prompt-injection defenses are hard to measure and benchmark
problem: Teams cannot tell which injection defenses work, detectors miss style-based and role-confusion attacks, and no agreed threat model exists.
who: teams deploying agents and security buyers
current_solutions: Validation layers outside the model, threat modeling with attacker-controlled LLM
opportunity: Build an independent benchmark and scanner that scores agent apps for injection resistance.

title: Audio in generated video is poor and misaligned
problem: Native audio from video models is muffled, garbled or disconnected from on-screen action, lip-sync is hard, and emotion tags are spoken literally.
current_solutions: Separate audio upscale or replacement passes, LTX Studio with ElevenLabs lip-sync, Kling 3.0 native audio, custom ComfyUI workflows
opportunity: Build a post-production tool that aligns, replaces and enhances audio in generated video with guided prompting.

title: Memory-efficient and in-memory inference hardware
problem: LLM inference is bottlenecked by data movement and expensive HBM, so people explore compute-in-memory, baked-in weights, and cheaper memory tiers.
who: hardware researchers and cost-constrained inference builders
current_solutions: IBM NorthPole, Taalas, FPGAs, Optane with llama.cpp offload, many-channel DDR4 Xeons, Engram-style RAM tables.
opportunity: Build inference software exploiting tiered memory with deterministic access patterns to run huge models on cheap hardware.

title: Frank expert advice on medical, legal and money topics
problem: Users want knowledgeable-friend advice without hedging, but chatbots are confidently wrong on high-stakes topics.
current_solutions: Claude for repairs, ChatGPT for budgeting, professional review
opportunity: Build vertical advisory apps with guardrails and professional review.

title: LLM cost attribution per request, task and user
problem: Provider dashboards show only aggregate totals and observability tools show flat spans, so cost cannot be traced to a request, agent loop, retry storm or user.
who: teams operating LLM apps and agents
current_solutions: OpenRouter Broadcast to Langfuse and Datadog, Tailscale Aperture, per-route cost proxies, custom metrics
opportunity: Build APM-style tracing that rolls token cost up to request, task, user and agent loop and flags retry and context drift.

title: Biosecurity screening and misuse
problem: DNA synthesis orders need screening and bio-capability risks lack misuse prevention tooling.
opportunity: Build synthesis order screening and access tracking.

title: AI game assets lack consistency and game-ready quality
problem: Image generators can't reliably deliver transparent backgrounds, true pixel art, seamless tiles or consistent sprites, so assets need heavy manual cleanup.
current_solutions: gpt-image-2 chroma-key sprite sheets, agents calling image APIs, Claude Code with Gemini and Seedance, AI art as placeholders
opportunity: Build an asset pipeline producing style-locked sprites, tiles and animation sheets with background removal, pixel snapping and spatial QA.

title: Scarcity of authentic real-world AI training data
problem: Models are bottlenecked on authentic, niche or expert data and the data market is opaque.
who: AI labs and specialized model builders
current_solutions: Protege AI, expert data vendors, buying defunct startups' archives, Wikimedia Enterprise
opportunity: Build a marketplace for licensed, provenance-tracked real-world datasets.

title: Robotaxi, wearables and robot dog hype
problem: Robotaxis, AI wearables and consumer robots show limited coverage or weak utility.

title: Provider policies and lock-in hit agent builders
problem: Providers revoke access, restrict third-party use of subscriptions and change policies opaquely.
current_solutions: OpenRouter, BYO-key harnesses

title: Clinical AI needs HIPAA compliance, validation and interpretability
